news|last=Lane|first=Barnaby|date=7 February 2022|title=An Olympic speed skater says she was put in an ambulance at 3 a.m. after being released from quarantine, then cried 'like crazy'|url=https://www.businessinsider.in/sports/news/an-olympic-speed-skater-says-she-was-put-in-an-ambulance-at-3-a-m-after-being-released-from-quarantine-then-cried-like-crazy/articleshow/89413365.cms|work=[[Insider (news website)|Insider]]|location=New York City, New York, U.S.|access-date=11 February 2022|archive-date=8 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220208214901/https://www.businessinsider.in/sports/news/an-olympic-speed-skater-says-she-was-put-in-an-ambulance-at-3-a-m-after-being-released-from-quarantine-then-cried-like-crazy/articleshow/89413365.cms|url-status=live}}

With China's Zero-COVID policy, there were issues raised about the process of quarantine at the games. On 2 February, Belgian skeleton athlete Kim Meylemans posted on social media and was in tears about the conditions she faced while in quarantine.{{cite news|last=Panja|first=Tariq|date=2 February 2022|title=Confusion, frustration and tears: a Belgian Olympian's day in isolation|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/02/02/sports/olympics/kim-meylemans-olympics-covid-quarantine.html|work=[[New York Times]]|location=New York City, New York, U.S.|access-date=|archive-date=9 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209021501/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/02/02/sports/olympics/kim-meylemans-olympics-covid-quarantine.html|url-status=live}}{{cite news|last=Reynolds|first=Tim|date=3 February 2022|title=Olympian moved to village after tearful video in isolation|url=https://apnews.com/article/winter-olympics-kim-meylemans-covid-isolation-8ccaf121249292e846a31a896c0250e4|work=Associated Press|location=New York City, New York, U.S|access-date=11 February 2022|archive-date=9 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209023741/https://apnews.com/article/winter-olympics-kim-meylemans-covid-isolation-8ccaf121249292e846a31a896c0250e4|url-status=live}} According to Newsweek and ''Time'', the hotels' conditions appeared to have improved after the athletes' complaints were made public.{{Cite magazine |last=CHAD DE GUZMAN |date=February 21, 2022 |title=What We Learned About COVID-19 Rules at the 2022 Olympics |url=https://time.com/6149800/beijing-2022-covid-19-olympics/ |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220309002003/https://time.com/6149800/beijing-2022-covid-19-olympics/ |archive-date=March 9, 2022 |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |language=en}}

There were some complaints about the food served outside of quarantine. Germany's alpine coach Christian Schweiger called the catering "extremely questionable" for not having hot meals but he echoed athletes from several nations that the food at the nearby Athletes' Village was great. The US and South Korean teams elected to bring their own food.{{Cite news |last=Keh |first=Andrew |date=2022-02-16 |title=A Quest for the Best Food Inside the Beijing Winter Olympics Bubble |language=en-US |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/02/16/sports/olympics/chinese-food-bubble-hotels.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220305003000/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/02/16/sports/olympics/chinese-food-bubble-hotels.html |archive-date=2022-03-05 |issn=0362-4331}} Austrian skier Matthias Mayer said that Kitzbuehel would have offered "the best of the best" but also that a hot meal right before a race might not bring out top performances.{{cite news|last=O'Connor|first=Philip|date=6 February 2022|title=Alpine skiing-Cold food riles Germany coach, U.S. bring own pasta|url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/alpine-skiing-cold-food-riles-germany-coach-us-bring-own-pasta-2022-02-06/|work=[[Reuters]]|location=London, United Kingdom|access-date=11 February 2022|archive-date=10 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210205459/https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/alpine-skiing-cold-food-riles-germany-coach-us-bring-own-pasta-2022-02-06/|url-status=live}}{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/cold-food-winter-olympics-riles-germany-coach|title=Cold food at Winter Olympics riles Germany coach|date=6 February 2022|website=www.nbcolympics.com|publisher=[[NBC]]|access-date=12 February 2022|archive-date=9 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220209015440/https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/cold-food-winter-olympics-riles-germany-coach|url-status=live}}

Other complaints included low temperatures and related safety concerns. Sweden's Frida Karlsson nearly collapsed at the conclusion of the women's skiathlon cross-country race. Afterwards, her team considered requesting that races held in afternoons and evenings for European TV audiences be moved to earlier during the day.{{cite news|date=8 February 2022|title=Beijing 2022: Winter Olympics hit by deluge of complaints from athletes|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-60298184|work=[[BBC News]]|location=London, United Kingdom|access-date=11 February 2022|archive-date=10 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210045217/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-china-60298184|url-status=live}} Some athletes resorted to putting tape on their faces and noses to protect them from the bitter cold.{{cite news|last=Dicker|first=Ron|date=10 February 2022|title=Athletes Are Taping Their Faces At Winter Olympics But Maybe They Shouldn't|url=https://www.huffpost.com/entry/tape-face-winter-olympics_n_620507c6e4b04af87f3967b0|work=[[HuffPost]]|location=New York City, New York, U.S.|access-date=11 February 2022|archive-date=10 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220210202323/https://www.huffpost.com/entry/tape-face-winter-olympics_n_620507c6e4b04af87f3967b0|url-status=live}} Heavy snowfall disrupted a number of competition and training events on 13 February. Thirty-three skiers did not finish their first run of the men's giant slalom. Henrik Kristoffersen of Norway said that he "couldn't see shit." Switzerland's Loic Meillard said, "It's not what I was hoping for but it's part of the game ... we've raced in conditions like that before."{{cite news |last1=Diaz |first1=Jaclyn |title=(Real) snow disrupts events at the Beijing Winter Olympics |url=https://www.npr.org/2022/02/13/1080446506/weather-snow-disrupts-events-at-the-beijing-olympics |publisher=NPR |date=13 February 2022 |language=en |access-date=16 January 2023 |archive-date=4 May 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220504155613/https://www.npr.org/2022/02/13/1080446506/weather-snow-disrupts-events-at-the-beijing-olympics |url-status=live }}

The 2022 Winter Olympics, officially known as the XXIV Olympic Winter Games, was a winter multi-sport event held in Beijing, China, from 4 to 20 February. A total of 2,871 athletes from 91 nations participated in 109 events in seven sports across 15 disciplines.{{cite news |last1=Kesting |first1=Amanda |title=Colorado Sent More Athletes to the Winter Olympics Than More Than Half of the Countries Participating |url=https://www.9news.com/article/sports/olympics/colorado-winter-olympics-delegation-size/73-d466dee8-4ba6-454f-b6a1-d35292d61266 |access-date=13 February 2022 |agency=[[KUSA (TV)|KUSA]] |date=4 February 2022 |archive-date=9 April 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230409061404/https://www.9news.com/article/sports/olympics/colorado-winter-olympics-delegation-size/73-d466dee8-4ba6-454f-b6a1-d35292d61266 |url-status=live }}{{cite news |last1=Edmonds |first1=Charlotte |title=Here's a Guide to New Events Debuting at the Winter Olympics |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/beijing-2022-winter-olympics/heres-guide-new-events-debuting-winter-olympics |access-date=12 September 2022 |agency=[[NBC Sports Philadelphia]] |date=4 February 2022 |archive-date=17 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230217004939/https://www.nbcsports.com/philadelphia/beijing-2022-winter-olympics/heres-guide-new-events-debuting-winter-olympics |url-status=live }}

Overall 29 nations received at least one medal, and 23 of them won at least one gold medal. Athletes from Norway won the most medals overall, with 37, and the most gold medals, with 16. The latter record was the highest gold medal tally at a single Winter Games.{{cite news |last1=Stuhlbarg |first1=Nate |title=Norway Retains Title with most Medals at 2022 Winter Olympics |url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/norway-retains-title-most-medals-2022-winter-olympics |access-date=27 March 2022 |agency=[[NBC Sports]] |date=20 February 2022 |archive-date=20 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220220195122/https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/norway-retains-title-most-medals-2022-winter-olympics |url-status=live }} Host nation China won nine gold medals surpassing its gold medal tally of five during the 2010 winter edition.{{cite web |title=China, Japan Set New Medal Marks in Winter Olympics |url=https://ocasia.org/news/2816-china-japan-set-new-medal-marks-in-winter-olympics.html |publisher=[[Olympic Council of Asia]] |access-date=12 July 2022 |archive-date=17 February 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230217005811/https://ocasia.org/news/2816-china-japan-set-new-medal-marks-in-winter-olympics.html |url-status=live }} Athletes from that nation also won 15 medals overall, which eclipsed its record of 11 at both the 2006 and 2010 winter editions.{{cite news |last1=Stuhlbarg |first1=Nate |title=Norway Retains Title with Most Medals at 2022 Winter Olympics |url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/norway-retains-title-most-medals-2022-winter-olympics |access-date=27 March 2022 |agency=[[NBC Sports]] |date=20 February 2022 |archive-date=20 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220220195122/https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/norway-retains-title-most-medals-2022-winter-olympics |url-status=live }}

Biathletes Johannes Thingnes Bø, Quentin Fillon Maillet, and Marte Olsbu Røiseland, and cross-country skier Alexander Bolshunov won the most total medals at the games with five each.{{cite web |title=Beijing 2022 |url=https://www.teamgb.com/competitions/beijing-2022/6dWdXrzU85Vn1jF6ZC9Onl |publisher=[[British Olympic Association]] |access-date=26 February 2022 |archive-date=18 March 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220318145104/https://www.teamgb.com/competitions/beijing-2022/6dWdXrzU85Vn1jF6ZC9Onl |url-status=live }} Bø also earned the most gold medals with four.{{cite news |author=[[Agence France-Presse]] |title=Norwegian Biathlete Boe Gets Fourth Beijing Olympics Gold Medal |url-status=live }} Snowboarder Zoi Sadowski-Synnott of New Zealand won the first Winter Olympic gold medal for that nation.{{cite news |first1=Bryan Armen |last1=Graham |title=Zoi Sadowski-Synnott Wins New Zealand's First Ever Winter Olympic Gold |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2022/feb/05/zoi-sadowski-synnott-new-zealand-first-winter-olympic-gold-snowboard-beijing-2022-tess-coady silver, and Christoph Hafer and Matthias Sommer attaining bronze.{{cite news |last1=Levinsohn |first1=Dan |title=Germany Sweeps Two-Man Bobsled Podium with Friedrich, Lochner, Hafer |url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/recap-two-man-final-heats |access-date=19 February 2022 |agency=[[NBC Sports]] |date=15 February 2022 |archive-date=19 March 2023 PageTitle: Beijing Organizing Committee for the 2022 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games
Block: The Beijing Organizing Committee for the 2022 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games () (BOCWOG) was a public institution with legal person status, responsible for the organisation and coordination of all the preparations and delivery of the 2022 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games. It was located at the former steel plant of Shougang Corporation in Shijingshan District, Beijing. The executive board of the Beijing 2022 was its sole executive agency. The Chairman was Cai Qi, who is also a  CCP Politburo member and Beijing CCP secretary.

A total of six bids were initially submitted for the 2022 Winter Olympics. Four of the bids were subsequently withdrawn by 1 October 2014, citing either the high costs of hosting the Games or the lack of local support, leaving Almaty, Kazakhstan and Beijing, China as the only two remaining candidate cities.{{cite news|url=http://time.com/3462070/olympics-winter-2022/|title=Why Nobody Wants to Host the 2022 Winter Olympics|date=3 October 2014|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|access-date=20 September 2015|first=Lisa|last=Abend}} Beijing was then elected as the host city at the 128th IOC Session in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, on 31 July 2015.

On 3 October 2012, the IOC announced in a letter to the NOCs the bidding calendar for the 2022 Winter Olympics:{{cite news|url=http://www.olympic.org/content/the-ioc/bidding-for-the-games/current-bid-process-2022/|title= 2022 Olympic Winter Games Current bid process }}

On 15 November 2013, the IOC announced the list of the six applicant cities.{{cite news|url=http://www.olympic.org/news/rising-interest-in-olympic-winter-games-as-six-cities-bid-to-host-2022-games/217175|title=Rising interest in Olympic Winter Games as six cities bid to host 2022 Games|work=olympic.org|publisher=International Olympic Committee|date=15 November 2013}} On 7 July 2014, the IOC announced that there were three remaining applicant cities that would move on to the candidate phase; these were Almaty, Beijing and Oslo.

On 1 October 2014, Oslo withdrew its application after one of the country's governing political parties Høyre decided not to support the application.[https://www.si.com/more-sports/2014/10/01/norway-rejects-2022-winter-olympics "Norway government rejects 2022 Winter Olympics bid"], from ''Sports Illustrated'' 1 October 2014 The remaining two candidate cities were therefore Almaty and Beijing.{{cite news|url=http://www.olympic.org/news/first-ioc-executive-board-meeting-under-president-bach/218358|title=First IOC Executive Board meeting under President Bach|publisher=International Olympic Committee|work=olympic.org|date=10 December 2013}}{{cite news|title=Five bid cities submit application files to host 2022 Olympic Winter Games|url=http://www.olympic.org/news/five-bid-cities-submit-application-files-to-host-2022-olympic-winter-games/227355|work=olympic.org|publisher=International Olympic Committee|date=14 March 2014}}

Both of the candidate cities suggested hosting the Games between February 4–20, 2022. The Paralympics will be held from March 4–13. While another city suggested hosting the Games between February 11–27, 2022. The Paralympics will be held from March 11–20.

Since 2011, the National Olympic Committee of the Republic of Kazakhstan has been considering a bid for the 2022 games in Almaty, the former longtime capital city and still the largest city and financial centre of the country.{{cite web|url=http://www.gamesbids.com/eng/winter_olympic_bids/future_winter_bids/1216135536.html |title=Kazakhstan Considers 2022 Winter Games Bid |publisher=GamesBids.com |date=31 January 2011 |access-date=14 November 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131114010311/http://www.gamesbids.com/eng/winter_olympic_bids/future_winter_bids/1216135536.html |archive-date=14 November 2013 }}{{cite web|url=http://www.aroundtherings.com/articles/view.aspx?id=42105|title=Oslo Talks Public Support; Toronto Searches for Mascot; FEI Ousts Guadalajara|work=aroundtherings.com|access-date=2015-07-31|archive-date=2013-11-14|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131114001703/http://www.aroundtherings.com/articles/view.aspx?id=42105|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=http://en.tengrinews.kz/kazakhstan_news/Kazakhstan-to-bid-for-2022-winter-Olympic-Games--445/|title=Kazakhstan to bid for 2022 winter Olympic Games|publisher=En.tengrinews.kz|date=28 March 2011|access-date=14 November 2013}} Kazakhstan hosted the 2011 Asian Winter Games. Almaty will host 2017 Winter Universiade. The current Kazakh capital Astana considered to joint bid with Almaty but the idea was later declined. On 17 August 2013, Almaty announced they were bidding for the 2022 Games.[http://www.gamesbids.com/eng/winter_olympic_bids/future_winter_bids/1216136727.html Almaty Bids For 2022 Winter Olympic Games] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006122431/http://www.gamesbids.com/eng/winter_olympic_bids/future_winter_bids/1216136727.html |date=October 6, 2014 }} Under the slogan "Keeping it Real", Almaty has emphasized her traditional winter setting with tall mountains and plenty of natural snow coverage as well as compactness — most venues are within half an hour's travel through Alpine scenery.[https://web.archive.org/web/20190306131242/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/olympics/almaty-offers-traditional-winter-setting-in-2022-olympic-bid/2015/07/28/d2de145a-3505-11e5-b835-61ddaa99c73e_story.html Almaty offers traditional winter setting in 2022 Olympic bid], ''[[The Washington Post]]'', 2015/7/28[http://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2015/jul/26/almaty-2022-winter-olympic-bid-at-a-glance/?page=all Almaty 2022 Winter Olympic bid at a glance], ''[[The Washington Times]]'', 2015/7/26

Presenting Kazakhstan's bid at the final event in Kuala Lumpur, Prime Minister of Kazakhstan Karim Massimov made a powerful speech with a key message that Almaty was "not a risk choice for 2022", but "a golden opportunity to prove that smaller advancing nations can successfully host the winter games". He called to the IOC core values saying that letting Almaty host the Games was "a golden opportunity to showcase the real long-term power of Olympic legacy for a region that has never hosted the Games".[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v6kx0YUXJGg Speech made by Karim Massimov before the final voting in Kuala Lumpur on July 31]
In the final voting Almaty lost to Beijing by only 4 votes.

On 5 November 2013, the Chinese Olympic Committee announced that it would submit a bid for Beijing to host the 2022 Winter Olympics. Beijing (where the indoor ice sports and the ceremonies would take place), was the host city of the 2008 Summer Olympics. Zhangjiakou would host the outdoor snow events.{{cite web|url=http://www.insidethegames.biz/olympics/winter-olympics/2022/1016809-beijing-and-zhangjiakou-launch-a-joint-bid-to-host-the-2022-winter-olympic-games|title=Beijing and Zhangjiakou launch joint bid to host 2022 Winter Olympic Games|work=insidethegames.biz|date=5 November 2013 }}

Before the final voting in Kuala Lumpur Beijing's bid was presented by Yang Lan, a renowned former CCTV host, who said sports and fitness were becoming a new fashion trend in China. In her speech she focused on China's economy and its ability to support every commitment it made "protecting long time financial viability and the reputation of the Games".[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=0uW5JT2_G2o Speech of Yang Lan before the final voting in Luala Lumpur on July 31]

On 6 November 2013, the Norwegian Olympic and Paralympic Committee and Confederation of Sports announced that Oslo would be submitted as the Norwegian candidate for the 2022 Winter Olympic Games. Oslo last hosted the 1952 Winter Olympics, and Norway last hosted the 1994 Winter Olympics in Lillehammer.{{cite news|last=Mackay|first=Duncan|title=Exclusive: Oslo confirm they will bid for 2022 Winter Olympics and Paralympics|url=http://www.insidethegames.biz/olympics/winter-olympics/2022/1016831-exclusive-oslo-confirm-they-will-bid-for-2022-winter-olympics-and-paralympics|access-date=6 November 2013|date=6 November 2013}} On 1 October 2014 the Conservative Party decided that they would not support a bid for the games citing costs and lack of public support.{{Cite news|title = Oslo Withdraws Bid to Host 2022 Winter Games, Citing Cost|url = https://www.nytimes.com/2014/10/02/sports/oslo-withdraws-bid-for-2022-olympics-citing-high-cost-of-games.html|newspaper = The New York Times|date = 2014-10-01|access-date = 2015-09-18|issn = 0362-4331|first = Lynn|last = Zinser}} A vast number of polls were conducted, and since April 2014 support had varied between 24% and 37%.{{Cite web|title = OL-stemningen|url = http://www.minervanett.no/ol-stemningen/|website = Minerva|access-date = 2015-09-18}} The days leading up to the deliberation in the Conservative Party had consisted of a series of negative developments for the bid. Those negative developments included the Centre Party saying "no" through a grass root vote,{{Cite web|title = Senterpartiet sier nei til OL i Oslo 2022 - Senterpartiet|url = http://www.senterpartiet.no/meny-forside/senterpartiet-sier-nei-til-ol-i-oslo-2022-article84533-12919.html|website = www.senterpartiet.no|access-date = 2015-09-18|url-status = dead|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20160204172514/http://www.senterpartiet.no/meny-forside/senterpartiet-sier-nei-til-ol-i-oslo-2022-article84533-12919.html|archive-date = 2016-02-04}} a poll showing that even within the Norwegian Confederation of Sports the majority of members opposed the bid,{{Cite web|title = Idrettsmedlemmer splittet om OL|url = http://www.nrk.no/norge/idrettsmedlemmer-splittet-om-ol-1.11959889|access-date = 2015-09-18|last = NRK| date=30 September 2014 }} an external revision which clarified that the newly suggested cheaper budget was unrealistic{{Cite web|title = Billig-OL dyrere enn antatt|url = http://www.nettavisen.no/na24/billig-ol-dyrere-enn-antatt/8492490.html|access-date = 2015-09-18|last = NTB| date=30 September 2014 }} and public scrutiny on IOC´s 7000 pages of demands.{{Cite news|title = The Olympics that no-one wants?| work=BBC Sport |url = https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/winter-olympics/29455789|access-date = 2015-09-18}}

Norway rejected the Olympic committee's application for government funding to hold the event in Norway after the private organization IOC made a large number of demands which caused a scandal in Norway. The demands notably included "diva-like demands for luxury treatment" for the IOC members themselves, such as special lanes on all roads only to be used by IOC members, a cocktail reception at the Royal Palace with drinks paid for by the royal family, car and drivers for all IOC members, adjusted traffic lights, free cell phones, seasonal fruits, and all "OL-shaped" and "Olympic Appearance” furniture.{{Cite web |title=IOC demands smiles, ridiculous perks ahead of 2022 Olympic bid |url=https://www.cbssports.com/general/news/ioc-demands-smiles-ridiculous-perks-ahead-of-2022-olympic-bid/ |access-date=2022-05-28 |website=CBSSports.com |date=October 2014 |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Mathis-Lilley |first=Ben |date=2014-10-02 |title=The IOC Demands That Helped Push Norway Out of Winter Olympic Bidding Are Hilarious |url=https://slate.com/news-and-politics/2014/10/ioc-demands-oslo-drops-bid-after-over-the-top-list-of-requirements.html |access-date=2022-05-28 |website=Slate Magazine |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=2014-10-02 |title=IOC hits out as Norway withdraws Winter Olympic bid |work=Financial Times |url=https://www.ft.com/content/d8938ffc-4a04-11e4-8de3-00144feab7de |access-date=2022-05-28}} The IOC also demanded "control over all advertising space throughout Oslo during the Games, to be used exclusively by official sponsors." Several commentators pointed out that such demands were unheard of in a western democracy; Slate described the IOC as a "notoriously ridiculous organization run by grifters and hereditary aristocrats."[http://www.slate.com/blogs/the_slatest/2014/10/02/ioc_demands_oslo_drops_bid_after_over_the_top_list_of_requirements.html The IOC Demands That Helped Push Norway Out of Winter Olympic Bidding Are Hilarious], Slate{{cite web |title=IOC reportedly made some ridiculous demands to help push Oslo out of 2022 Winter Olympics bidding |website=[[National Post]] |url=https://nationalpost.com/sports/olympics/ioc-reportedly-made-some-ridiculous-demands-to-help-push-oslo-out-of-2022-winter-olympics-bidding}}[https://www.vg.no/sport/ol-2022/ioc-krever-gratis-sprit-paa-stadion-og-cocktail-fest-med-kongen/a/23306598/ IOC krever gratis sprit på stadion og cocktail-fest med Kongen]

On 7 November 2013, the Polish Olympic Committee announced they submitted a bid to the IOC for the 2022 Winter Olympics, together with Zakopane, Poland, and Jasná, a village in central Slovakia, near the Polish border.{{cite web|title=Polish Olympic Committee to Bid for 2022 Games|url=http://www.pkol.pl/pl/pages/news/6159|work=Polish Olympic Committee|access-date=7 November 2013}}{{cite web|url=http://www.insidethegames.biz/olympics/winter-olympics/2022/1016844-poland-and-slovakia-confirm-joint-bid-for-2022-winter-olympics-and-paralympics|title=Poland and Slovakia confirm joint bid for 2022 Winter Olympics and Paralympics|work=insidethegames.biz|date=7 November 2013 }} If the bid had been successful, it would have been the first time either Poland or Slovakia hosted the Olympics.{{cite web|last=Hula|first=Ed|title=Krakow Bidding for 2022|url=http://aroundtherings.com/articles/view.aspx?id=44968|publisher=Around the Rings}} Zakopane previously bid to host the 2006 Winter Olympics but failed to become a candidate. Kraków's bid was submitted to a local referendum held on 25 May 2014, which had a negative result. After that Kraków discontinued the application on 26 May 2014.{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/2014/05/26/krakow-withdraws-2022-winter-olympics-bid/9588543/|title=Krakow withdraws 2022 Winter Olympics bid|author=AP|date=26 May 2014|work=USA TODAY}}

The National Olympic Committee of Ukraine officially submitted a bid for Lviv to host the 2022 Winter Olympic Games on 5 November 2013.{{cite web|title=Lviv Officially drink For 2022 Winter Olympics |url=http://www.gamesbids.com/eng/winter_olympic_bids/future_winter_bids/1216136800.html |work=GamesBids.com |access-date=5 November 2013 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131105183155/http://www.gamesbids.com/eng/winter_olympic_bids/future_winter_bids/1216136800.html |archive-date=5 November 2013 }} On 30 June 2014, however, the IOC announced that Lviv would "turn its attention to an Olympic bid for 2026, and not continue with its application for 2022. The decision comes as a result of the 2013–2015 Ukrainian crisis" which seriously influences Lviv and the country.{{cite web|url=http://www.olympic.org/news/ioc-statement-on-2022-bidding-process/234698|title=IOC statement on 2022 Bidding Process|work=olympic.org}}

On 11 November 2013, the Swedish Olympic Committee announced that it had submitted a bid,{{cite web|title=Stockholm bids for 2022 Winter Olympics|url=http://www.sbs.com.au/news/article/2013/11/12/stockholm-bids-2022-winter-olympics|work=SBS News|access-date=11 November 2013}} but on 17 January 2014, Stockholm dropped the bid due to lack of political support.{{cite web|url=http://www.thelocal.se/20140117/stockholm-drops-bid-for-2022-winter-olympics|title=Stockholm drops bid for 2022 Winter Olympics|work=thelocal.se}} Åre, about  from Stockholm, was scheduled to host the alpine skiing events. Stockholm previously hosted the 1912 Summer Olympics and hosted equestrian events of the 1956 Summer Olympics, but this was the first time the Swedish capital had bid for the Winter Olympics. Had it won, it would have been the first city to host both the Summer Olympics and the Winter Olympics, a distinction that ultimately went to Beijing.

PageTitle: Bing Dwen Dwen and Shuey Rhon Rhon
Block: Bing Dwen Dwen is a giant panda with a suit of ice, a heart of gold and a love of winter sports. "Bing" means ice and embodies purity and strength, the characteristics of the Winter Olympics. "Dwen Dwen", which means health, liveliness and cuteness, conforms to the overall image of pandas and symbolizes the strength, tenacity and inspiring Olympic spirit of Winter Olympic athletes. The colorful ring around Bing Dwen Dwen's face is inspired by the "ice ribbon" of the national speed skating hall of the Beijing Winter Olympics. The heart on Bing Dwen Dwen's palm is a warm welcome to friends all over the world.{{cite web |title=Beijing 2022 |url=https://www.beijing2022.cn/a/20190917/007476.htm |website=Explanation of the mascot of Beijing 2022 Olympics |access-date=9 February 2022 |archive-date=18 September 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190918173106/https://www.beijing2022.cn/a/20190917/007476.htm |url-status=dead }} Bing Dwen Dwen's full-body "shell", which helps the panda to skate, snowboard and ski alongside the Olympic athletes, is a tribute to embracing new technologies for a future with infinite possibilities, the bright colours of the halo around its face are a representation of the latest advanced technologies of the ice and snow sport tracks at the Games, while the heart on its left palm symbolises China's hospitality for athletes and spectators at the Winter Olympics.{{cite web |title=Beijing 2022 Mascot |url=https://olympics.com/en/beijing-2022/mascot |website=Beijing 2022 |publisher=International Olympic Committee |access-date=10 February 2022}} Some netizens believe Bing Dwen Dwen's design may have also been inspired by the traditional Chinese winter treat tanghulu (糖葫芦) as the suit of ice resembles the clear candy coating.

PageTitle: Bing Dwen Dwen and Shuey Rhon Rhon
Block: Shuey Rhon Rhon is an anthropomorphic Chinese lantern. Lanterns represent harvest, celebration, warmth and light. The wishful shape at the top symbolizes auspicious happiness. The continuous pattern of the dove of peace and the Temple of Heaven symbolize the peaceful friendship and highlights the characteristics of the place where the events are held. The decorative pattern incorporates the traditional Chinese paper-cutting art. The snow on the face represents the meaning of "a fall of seasonable snow gives promise of a fruitful year" (瑞雪兆丰年). It also reflects the anthropomorphic design and highlights the mascot's cuteness.

PageTitle: Bing Dwen Dwen and Shuey Rhon Rhon
Block: Bing Dwen Dwen is the main Olympic mascot. Shuey Rhon Rhon is the Paralympic mascot.

PageTitle: Bing Dwen Dwen and Shuey Rhon Rhon
Block: Bing Dwen Dwen was designed by Cao Xue (曹雪), a chief designer at Guangzhou Academy of Fine Arts. Cao Xue stated that during the months leading up to the games, he and his design team designing and modifying the mascot and once gave up the idea of a panda mascot due to it prevalence.{{Cite web |date=2022-02-09 |title=Panda 'phenomenon' Bing Dwen Dwen surprises Beijing Olympics mascot designer |url=https://hongkongfp.com/2022/02/10/panda-phenomenon-bing-dwen-dwen-surprises-beijing-olympics-mascot-designer/ |access-date=2022-03-03 |website=Hong Kong Free Press HKFP |language=en-GB}} He also expressed his surprise that the demand for the mascot was so high.{{Cite web |last=Tan |first=Huileng |date=February 7, 2022 |title=People queued for hours in the freezing cold for Beijing Winter Olympics panda mascot merch only to be told they've been sold out |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/people-queued-hours-freezing-beijing-winter-olympics-panda-mascot-2022-2 |access-date=2022-03-03 |website=Business Insider |language=en-US}}

PageTitle: Bing Dwen Dwen and Shuey Rhon Rhon
Block: Shuey Rhon Rhon was designed by Jiang Yufan (姜玉凡), an undergraduate majoring in product design at the Jilin Art Institute of Design. Jiang Yufan first submitted mascot designs based on a deer, and a combination of a Chinese knot and a dumpling, but after suggestions from her professors she altered the design to be a combination of a Chinese knot and a red lantern.{{Cite web |last1=Ye |first1=Zizhen |last2=Han |first2=Junhong |date=February 22, 2022 |title=Hard work, many revisions made Paralympic mascot |url=https://global.chinadaily.com.cn/a/202202/22/WS62143df2a310cdd39bc88193.html |access-date=2022-03-03 |website=global.chinadaily.com.cn}}

PageTitle: Bing Dwen Dwen and Shuey Rhon Rhon
Block: It was announced on 10 February that 500 epic boxes that would include multiple designs of Bing Dwen Dwen would go on sale the next day via nWayPlay. Each box would be priced at $99, with a maximum of five per purchase and would include three officially licensed digital pins with approved mascot art featuring different winter sports, the official emblem and a poster. Due to their popularity a second round of officially licensed NFTs were announced 17 February, the 200 legendary boxes would be priced at $349, with only one box per purchase. Each legendary box would include a work of art and two pincs.{{Cite web |last=Shen |first=Xinmei |date=2022-02-11 |title=Beijing's Olympics mascot NFTs to open for sale, but not in China |url=https://www.scmp.com/tech/tech-trends/article/3166727/beijings-beloved-olympics-panda-mascot-has-its-own-nfts-they-are |access-date=2022-03-03 |website=South China Morning Post |language=en}}{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2022-02-21 |title=Collectors seek Bing Dwen Dwen NFTs |url=https://www.manilatimes.net/2022/02/21/business/foreign-business/collectors-seek-bing-dwen-dwen-nfts/1833708 |access-date=2022-03-03 |website=The Manila Times |language=en}}

The 2022 Winter Olympics closing ceremony was held at the Beijing National Stadium in Beijing on 20 February 2022. As mandated by the Olympic Charter, the proceedings are expected to combine the formal ceremonial closing of this international sporting event (including closing speeches, hoisting of the flags, the parade of athletes, and the handover of the Olympic flag) with an artistic spectacle to showcase the culture and history of the current and next host nation (Italy) for the 2026 Winter Olympics in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo.{{cite web|date=2021-09-30|title=Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games Beijing 2022 - Updates on Spectators, Vaccination And COVID-19 Countermeasures - Olympic News|url=https://olympics.com/ioc/news/olympic-and-paralympic-winter-games-beijing-2022-updates-on-spectators-vaccination-and-covid-19-countermeasures|access-date=2021-10-10|website=International Olympic Committee|language=en}}

The closing ceremony was directed by film director and producer Zhang Yimou, who also directed the opening ceremonies of the 2022 Winter Olympics and previously directed and produced the opening and closing ceremonies of the 2008 Summer Olympics.{{cite web|url=http://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/olympics/2022/02/17/everything-you-need-to-know-about-the-closing-ceremonies-of-the-beijing-olympics|title=Everything You Need To Know About The Closing Ceremonies Of The Beijing Olympics|website=WashingtonPost.com|date=February 17, 2022|accessdate=February 17, 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2022/feb/20/winter-olympics-day-16-gb-in-womens-curling-final-mens-ice-hockey-live|title=Winter Olympics day 16: GB win women's curling gold before closing ceremony – as it happened|date=20 February 2022|work=Guardian|accessdate=21 February 2022}}
According to Zhao Weidong head of the 2022 Olympic organising committee's media department the theme of the closing ceremony will be:

As stated by Zhang Yimou, somewhere during the closing ceremony will re-create a moment from the opening ceremony of the 2008 Summer Olympics, as for the Beijing National Stadium being the venue for the ceremonies of both Summer and Winter Olympics.

Source:{{cite web |title=Beijing 2022 Winter Olympic Games Closing Ceremony Programme List |url=https://twitter.com/CGTNSportsScene/status/1495347623221350401/photo/1 |website=Twitter |publisher=CGTN Sports scene |access-date=20 February 2022}}
At 8:00pm China Standard Time, Chinese President Xi Jinping and International Olympic Committee President Thomas Bach entered the stadium.

As the closing ceremony takes place five days after the Lantern Festival, which is the final day of the Chinese New Year celebrations, a performance was held to celebrate and promote the culture of the Chinese New Year through lanterns. Children danced and played with lanterns while interacting with the large snowflake cauldron in the center of the stadium. Their movement formed the emblem of the 2022 Winter Olympics. The lanterns were shaped like snowflakes to commemorate the overlap of both the Winter Olympics and the Chinese New Year celebration as well as to highlight the tradition of playing with lanterns during the Lantern Festival.

Continuing from the lantern performance, twelve sleds shaped in the form of Chinese zodiac animals, namely the rat, ox, tiger, rabbit, dragon, snake, horse, goat, monkey, rooster, dog, and pig, carved out a Chinese knot on the floor, joining the children with lanterns in continuing the celebration of the Chinese New Year. The zodiac animals represent the interlinkage of the Chinese calendar and its solar terms. Animations performed by ribbons wrapped around the giant snowflake cauldron to form a hybrid combination of the Chinese knot and the lantern. The flags of the 91 competing nations entered the stadium first, followed by all the athletes who were still in Beijing marching in together as one group accompanied by an arrangement of Beethoven's Ode to Joy. The athletes gathered on the knot, symbolizing the Chinese culture of family reunion for the Chinese New Year.

First, the Greek flag was raised while the Greek national anthem is played. The Olympic flag was then lowered and folded while the Olympic Hymn was sung in Greek. Afterwards, the flag was passed from the mayor of Beijing, Chen Jining, to IOC president Thomas Bach, who then hand it over to the mayors of Milan, Giuseppe Sala, and Cortina d'Ampezzo, Gianpietro Ghedina. This was followed by the raising of the flag of Italy and the playing of its anthem sing by the know italian singer Malika Ayane.During the Italian national anthem, a projection of stars (representing the 7,904 comuni of the country) formed the outline of Italy. The Olympic flag will be raised again on January 19, 2024 for the opening ceremonies of the 2024 Winter Youth Olympics in Gangwon Province, South Korea

As Olympic tradition dictates,but now with an innovation, because for the first time in history, an edition of the Olympic Games will officially have two host cities. Since the italian cities of Milan and Cortina D'Ampezzo will host the next edition of the Winter Olympic Games scheduled for 2026.The two host cities took a shortcut on some concepts that Beijing based the organization and management of the edition that was ending and presented a 10-minute show called "Duality, Together". Unlike the pompous and exuberant shows traditionally presented by the world-know Italian producer Marco Balich, this time the COVID-19 pandemics led a elaboration of a more simple and sincere act that only needed 6 people and approximately 90% was produced in the city of Beijing itself based in an idea called "the less, is the better"{{cite news |last1=Ip |first1=Cyrus |last2=Lau |first2=Jack |title=Winter Olympics: 5 things to watch out for at the Beijing 2022 closing ceremony |url=https://www.asiaone.com/china/winter-olympics-5-things-watch-out-beijing-2022-closing-ceremony |access-date=20 February 2022 |agency=Asian One |publisher=South China Morning Post |date=20 February 2022}}

This segment presented by Milan-Cortina coincided with duality, one of the pillars of Far Eastern culture and the Beijing 2022 slogan "Together for a shared future", the slogan of the 2022 Winter Olympics. According to Christian Milici (MCO2026 Head of Events), they aimed to celebrate the harmony which links two cities (Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo) that are very seemingly different, but are in constant dialogue with each other.{{cite news |last1=Elbaba |first1=Julia |title=Italy Introduces 'Duality, Together' in Milano Cortina 2026 at Handover Ceremony |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/milano-cortina-2022-flag-handover-133701374.html |access-date=20 February 2022 |agency=NBC |publisher=Yahoo Sports |date=20 February 2022 |archive-date=6 April 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220406063500/https://sports.yahoo.com/milano-cortina-2022-flag-handover-133701374.html |url-status=dead }} Because of this concept, the segment was focused on the harmony between humanity and nature as the main life duality. The segment started with two children with the names of the host cities on each of their backs rolling and hugging a inflated vinyl plastic globe, representing the two next host cities inviting the world for the 2026 games and a historical link between Beijing and Milan, the Silk Road (a historical important trading route traced by Marco Polo which was the first registered link between Europe and Asia). After this walk, the first film depicted two dancer trekking across the host cities: the man was running in the urban landscape of Milan and a woman was running in the snowy mountains of Cortina d'Ampezzo. After the first film, the two then the two met on the LED stage set up in the center of the Beijing National Stadium. They presented a joint modern dance routine to represent the history and the cultural aspects of Italy. After the segment, a second film was shown depicting various athletes holding several Italian flags and flags with the 2026 Winter Olympics logo. It then shows several open-aired meetings across the country as Frecce Tricolori flies over Venice (main hotspot from Veneto, the region where Cortina is located) and the Italian Alps and introduced the two host regions, Lombardy and Veneto.{{cite news |author1= Michael Houston |title=Bach calls on leaders to find peace as Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics close
|url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1119560/beijing-2022-olympics-closing-ceremony |accessdate=20 February 2022|work=Inside the games |date=2022-02-20}}

Along the final speech and remarks made by Cai Qi, president and chairman of the Beijing Organizing Committee for the 2022 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games, the IOC President Thomas Bach formally declared the games closed, praising them as excellent and unforgettable, as per the Olympic Charter he invited in French the youth of the world to meet again in Milan and Cortina D'Ampezzo in four years time.{{cite web|url=http://sg.news.yahoo.com/ioc-president-thomas-bach-declares-beijing-winter-olympic-games-closed|title=IOC President Thomas Bach Declares Beijing Winter Olympic Games Closed|website=Yahoo.com|date=20 February 2022|accessdate=20 February 2022}}{{Dead link|date=July 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}

Following the declaration of the closing of the Games, a video was shown of Beijing citizens and Winter Games volunteers bidding farewell to their international guests. It concluded with Olympic mascot Bing Dwen Dwen waving to a snowflake as it flies toward the sky.

The Olympic flame, burning in torch 
docked at its base during the opening ceremony in the middle of a giant snowflake-shaped cauldron,was descending while one of the most striking scenes from the opening ceremony of the 2008 Summer Olympics was being reproduced (when the Olympic rings were formed on a carpet of LEDs that was suspended) gradually extinguished while "You and Me", the theme song of the 2008 Summer Olympics, was sampled when the snow flame was near to touch the ground and
and was it slowly faded away  extinguished,after the last after the last sparks burn out and it goes out for good,"Snowflakes", the theme song of the 2022 Winter Olympics, which was sung by the Beijing Philharmonic Choir (北京愛樂合唱團) started to play. This segmenr was written to highlight the fact that the city made the historical achievement of being the first city to host both the Summer and Winter Olympic Games, to end the ceremony as the Olympic Charter determines and a large display of fireworks started.As the fireworks exploded, the cast of the show began to sing "Auld Lang Syne".The song ended exactly at 21:40 CST and was the last moment of the ceremonies.

PageTitle: 2022 Winter Olympics closing ceremony flag bearers
Block: During the closing ceremony of the 2022 Winter Olympics in Beijing, China the flag bearers of 91 National Olympic Committees (NOCs) arrived into Beijing National Stadium on February 20. The flag bearers from each participating country entered the stadium informally in single file, and behind them marched all the athletes. The flags of each country were not necessarily carried by the same flag bearer as in the opening ceremony.

PageTitle: 2022 Winter Olympics closing ceremony flag bearers
Block: Athletes entered the stadium in an order dictated by the Olympic tradition. As the originator of the Olympics, the Greek flag bearer entered first.{{cite news|last2=Davis|first2=Scott|last1=Gaines|first1=Cork|date=9 February 2018|title=Why Greece always leads the parade of athletes at the Olympic opening ceremony and how the rest of the order is determined|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/greece-rio-olympics-opening-ceremony-parade-2016-8|work=[[Business Insider]]|location=New York City, New York, U.S.|access-date=15 January 2021}}  The country that will host the next Winter Olympics, Italy, marched before the host nation China entered, instead of entering between New Zealand and Serbia, according to the Chinese collation order.{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/ioc/news/future-olympic-hosts-to-gain-prominence-in-athletes-parades|title=Future Olympic hosts to gain prominence in athletes' parades|date=3 December 2019|website=www.olympics.com/|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=15 January 2021}}

PageTitle: 2022 Winter Olympics closing ceremony flag bearers
Block: Countries marched in order of the Chinese language.{{cite magazine|last=Steger|first=Isabella|date=4 February 2022|title=Here's the Order of Countries at the Beijing Olympics Opening Ceremony|url=https://time.com/6145111/order-of-countries-opening-ceremony-2022-olympics/|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|location=New York City, New York, US|access-date=8 February 2022}} The collation method used was based on the names as written in Simplified Chinese characters and is similar to that used in Chinese dictionaries. The names were sorted by the number of strokes in the first character of the name, then by the stroke order of the character (in the order 橫竖撇捺折, c.f. Wubi method), then the number of strokes and stroke order of the second character, then next character and so on.{{Cite news|last1=Mather|first1=Victor|last2=Buckley|first2=Chris|date=4 February 2022|title=The Chinese language determines the order of the Parade of Nations.|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/02/04/sports/opening-ceremony-order-of-countries.html|access-date=4 February 2022|issn=0362-4331}}  For example, this placed San Marino () in 28th position, just ahead of Kyrgyzstan () because the initial character for "San Marino" () is written in 5 strokes, while that for "Kyrgyzstan" () is written in 6 strokes.

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: The 2022 Winter Olympics took place between the 4 and 20 February 2022 and were hosted by in China in the capital city of Beijing. The country selected was the subject of various concerns and controversies about their cost, environmental impact, censorship, espionage, COVID-19, sportswashing, and human rights issues.

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: There have been diplomatic boycotts of the Olympics largely due to the human rights situation in China, and the Uyghur genocide in particular.{{Cite web|url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/12/24/national/japan-olympics-boycotts/|title=Japan not planning to send senior officials to Beijing Olympics|first1=Satoshi|last1=Sugiyama|first2=Jesse|last2=Johnson|date=24 December 2021|website=The Japan Times}} Additional reasons for diplomatic boycotts include China's alleged politicization of the games.

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: American sportscaster Bob Costas criticized the International Olympic Committee's (IOC) decision to award the games to China saying "The IOC deserves all of the disdain and disgust that comes their way for going back to China yet again" referencing China's human rights record.{{cite news |last1=Maruf |first1=Ramishah |title='Shameless,' former NBC host says of the Olympics returning to Beijing |url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/01/23/media/bob-costas-beijing-winter-olympics-reliable-sources/index.html |publisher=CNN |access-date=29 January 2022 |date=26 January 2022}}

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: After winning two gold medals and returning to his home country of Sweden skater Nils van der Poel criticized the IOC's selection of China as the host saying "I think it is extremely irresponsible to give it to a country that violates human rights as blatantly as the Chinese regime is doing." He had declined to criticize China before leaving for the games saying "I don't think it would be particularly wise for me to criticize the system I'm about to transition to, if I want to live a long and productive life."{{cite web |last1=Everington |first1=Keoni |title=Swedish skater says China's hosting of Olympics 'extremely irresponsible' amid human rights abuses |url=https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/4444098 |website=taiwannews.com.tw |date=15 February 2022 |publisher=Taiwan News |access-date=17 February 2022}}

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: Several cities withdrew their applications during the bidding process, citing the high costs or the lack of local support to host the 2022 games, leaving Almaty in Kazakhstan and Beijing as the only candidate cities by 1 October 2014.{{cite magazine |url=http://time.com/3462070/olympics-winter-2022/|title=Why Nobody Wants to Host the 2022 Winter Olympics because it causes lots of dogs to bark|date=3 October 2014|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |access-date=19 September 2015|first=Lisa|last=Abend|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150918021002/http://time.com/3462070/olympics-winter-2022/|archive-date=18 September 2015|url-status=live}}

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: The decision to bid for the Olympics was controversial in China (and outside), because Beijing itself, and especially some of the proposed outdoor venues, would not have reliable snowfall in winter for snow sports. Concerns have been raised that snow may need to be transported to the venues at great cost and with uncertain environmental consequences.{{cite magazine |last=Matt |first=Schiavenza |url=https://www.theatlantic.com/international/archive/2015/07/a-winter-olympics-in-a-city-without-snow/400250/ |title=A Winter Olympics in a City Without Snow |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190924045000/https://www.theatlantic.com/international/archive/2015/07/a-winter-olympics-in-a-city-without-snow/400250/ |archive-date=24 September 2019 |magazine=[[The Atlantic]] |date=31 July 2015}}{{cite news |first=Tom |last=Phillips |url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2015/jul/31/beijing-2022-winter-olympics-snow |title=Beijing promises to overcome lack of snow for 2022 Winter Olympics |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160619152046/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2015/jul/31/beijing-2022-winter-olympics-snow |archive-date=19 June 2016 |newspaper=[[The Guardian]] |date=31 July 2015}}

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: Some commentators alleged that one of the early promotional songs for the 2022 Winter Olympics, "The Snow and Ice Dance", sung by Sun Nan and Tan Jing, had suspicious similarities with "Let It Go", one of the songs from the 2013 Disney film, Frozen. A Chinese media outlet cited technical analysis of the two songs: both songs employ a piano as the major instrument, have similar prelude chords and an eight-beat introduction, and they run at almost exactly the same tempo.{{cite news|author1=Didi Kirsten Tatlow|title=To Some, Beijing Olympics Song Is Suspiciously Similar to Ballad From Disney's 'Frozen'|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2015/08/04/world/asia/to-some-song-of-beijing-games-is-suspiciously-similar-to-a-disney-ballad.html|access-date=5 August 2015|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=3 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150808044452/http://www.nytimes.com/2015/08/04/world/asia/to-some-song-of-beijing-games-is-suspiciously-similar-to-a-disney-ballad.html?_r=0|archive-date=8 August 2015|url-status=live}}{{cite news|last1=Jiang|first1=Steven|title=Is China's 2022 Winter Olympics song too much like 'Frozen's' 'Let It Go'?|url=http://edition.cnn.com/2015/08/04/china/china-winter-olympics-song-frozen/|access-date=5 August 2015|publisher=CNN|date=4 August 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150807060127/http://edition.cnn.com/2015/08/04/china/china-winter-olympics-song-frozen|archive-date=7 August 2015|url-status=live}}

After China had won the bid to host the 2022 Olympics, many Tibetan protesters had criticized the IOC for allowing China to host the games again due to its policies against Tibetans.{{cite news|title=Tibetan groups campaign against 2022 Olympics going to China|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/2015/07/28/tibetan-groups-campaign-against-2022-olympics-going-to-china/30771287/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191231085854/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/2015/07/28/tibetan-groups-campaign-against-2022-olympics-going-to-china/30771287/|archive-date=31 December 2019|access-date=5 November 2019|website=USA Today|language=en-US|agency=Associated Press}} In the aftermath of the 2019 leak of the Xinjiang papers, the 2019–20 Hong Kong protests, China's hostage diplomacy and the Uyghur genocide, calls were made for a boycott of the 2022 Games.{{cite web|last=Karlik|first=Evan|date=8 August 2019|title=The Case for Boycotting Beijing 2022|url=https://thediplomat.com/2019/08/the-case-for-boycotting-beijing-2022/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200503155623/https://thediplomat.com/2019/08/the-case-for-boycotting-beijing-2022/|archive-date=3 May 2020|access-date=27 November 2019|website=[[The Diplomat]]}}{{cite web|last=Westcott|first=Ben|date=2 December 2019|title=Huge leaks are exposing Xinjiang's re-education camps. But don't expect Beijing to back down|url=https://edition.cnn.com/2019/11/26/asia/china-xinjiang-leaks-analysis-intl-hnk/index.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200909151942/https://edition.cnn.com/2019/11/26/asia/china-xinjiang-leaks-analysis-intl-hnk/index.html|archive-date=9 September 2020|access-date=18 August 2020|publisher=CNN}}{{cite web|last=Montgomery|first=Marc|date=10 June 2020|title=Boycott the 2022 China Winter Olympics?|url=https://www.rcinet.ca/en/2020/06/10/boycott-the-2022-china-winter-olympics/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200818184356/https://www.rcinet.ca/en/2020/06/10/boycott-the-2022-china-winter-olympics/|archive-date=18 August 2020|access-date=18 August 2020|work=[[Radio Canada International]]}}{{cite web|author=Kenneth Bandler|date=17 August 2020|title=The Uyghers' plight is a humanitarian crisis. More must be done to help|url=https://www.jpost.com/opinion/the-uyghers-plight-is-a-humanitarian-crisis-more-must-be-done-to-help-638990|access-date=17 August 2020|website=[[The Jerusalem Post]]|quote='It is a genocide', says Turkel, adding that the 'purposeful prevention of population growth' is one of the legal definitions of genocide. 'In the last year, Uyghur population growth dropped by 24%, and in the previous three years by 84%.' ... If there is no significant change in Chinese government policy regarding the Uyghurs, Turkel would like to see the US boycott the Winter Olympics in Beijing in 2022.}} In November 2021 the disappearance of former Olympian Peng Shuai after she made allegations of sexual assault against Zhang Gaoli, former Vice Premier of China and a high ranking Chinese Communist Party (CCP) member, has put pressure on the International Olympic Committee.{{cite web|last1=Bjornson|first1=Greta|last2=Rubenstein|first2=Janine|title=Pressure Is 'Heightened' on China to Answer for Missing Tennis Star Peng Shuai's Whereabouts|url=https://people.com/sports/peng-shuai-missing-chinese-tennis-player-china-sexual-assault-people-every-day/|access-date=20 November 2021|work=People|date=20 November 2021}}

Some human rights organizations have called for a diplomatic boycott that would mean countries not sending their heads of state or high-ranking officials to the Olympics but still sending athletes.{{cite web|last1=Hillier|first1=Bianca|title=Human rights groups weigh boycott of 2022 Winter Olympics in Beijing|url=https://www.pri.org/stories/2020-11-12/human-rights-groups-weigh-boycott-2022-winter-olympics-beijing|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201125192022/https://www.pri.org/stories/2020-11-12/human-rights-groups-weigh-boycott-2022-winter-olympics-beijing|archive-date=25 November 2020|access-date=27 November 2020|website=pri.org|publisher=Public Radio International |date=12 November 2020}} In a 30 July 2020 letter, the World Uyghur Congress urged the IOC to reconsider holding the 2022 Winter Olympics in Beijing because of the Uyghur genocide.{{cite news|first=Stephanie |last=Nebehay|date=14 August 2020|title=Uighur group urges IOC to reconsider 2022 Beijing Winter Games venue|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-olympics-china-uighurs-idUSKCN25A1PG|access-date=18 August 2020}}{{cite news|title=Uighur group calls for China to lose 2022 Winter Olympics over 'genocide'|url=https://www.wionews.com/world/uighur-group-calls-for-china-to-lose-2022-winter-olympics-over-genocide-317143/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200809175242/https://www.wionews.com/world/uighur-group-calls-for-china-to-lose-2022-winter-olympics-over-genocide-317143|archive-date=9 August 2020|access-date=18 August 2020|publisher=[[WION (TV channel)|WION]] |agency=Agence France-Presse|date=31 July 2020}} The World Uyghur Congress does not support a full boycott; instead, they want athletes to use the games as a chance to raise awareness about the Uyghur genocide, similar to the way that athletes have raised the profile of the Black Lives Matter movement.{{cite news|last1=Wade|first1=Stephen|title=More questions on human rights for Beijing Winter Olympics|url=https://apnews.com/article/winter-olympics-juan-antonio-samaranch-beijing-2020-tokyo-olympics-china-d03b46950b26420664677b8d1aa8caa2|url-status=live|date=16 October 2020
|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201104122248/https://apnews.com/article/winter-olympics-juan-antonio-samaranch-beijing-2020-tokyo-olympics-china-d03b46950b26420664677b8d1aa8caa2|archive-date=4 November 2020|access-date=27 November 2020|website=apnews.com|agency=Associated Press}} The IOC met with activists in late 2020 about their request to move the Olympics.{{cite news|last=Wade|first=Stephen|date=14 March 2021|title=Explainer: What drives possible boycott of Beijing Olympics|work=Associated Press|url=https://apnews.com/article/race-and-ethnicity-winter-olympics-boycotts-tibet-hong-kong-7df9cfbfc0208bff14bc284e22d1e637|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210317235302/https://apnews.com/article/race-and-ethnicity-winter-olympics-boycotts-tibet-hong-kong-7df9cfbfc0208bff14bc284e22d1e637|archive-date=17 March 2021|access-date=20 March 2021}} In March 2021, the IOC president Thomas Bach opposed a boycott, which would also damage the IOC image and finances, and said that the IOC must stay out of politics. On 14 October 2021, the executive vice-president of the IOC, John Coates, said that the IOC would not challenge the Chinese government over the issue of the Uyghurs, stating that it was "not within the IOC's remit".{{Cite news|agency=Reuters|date=13 October 2021|title=IOC's Coates rules out pressuring China over human rights|language=en|work=Reuters|url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/iocs-coates-rules-out-pressuring-china-over-human-rights-2021-10-13/|access-date=15 October 2021}}

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics

Tom Cotton calls on Biden administration to boycott 2022 Winter Olympics in Beijing|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/congress/sen-tom-cotton-calls-biden-administration-boycott-2022-winter-olympics-n1284118|access-date=19 November 2021|publisher=NBC News|language=en |first1=Rebecca |last1=Shabad |date=18 November 2021}} Due to a change in the last version of the Olympic Charter, a full boycott by the United States, like the one at the 1980 Summer Olympics, could result in the most severe punishment, which is the suspension by the National Olympic Committee for 2 years of the Olympic Games, a similar situation to what happened with North Korea in the 2020 games.{{Cite news|last=Radnofsky|first=Louise|date=8 September 2021|title=North Korea Suspended From Olympics Until the End of 2022|language=en-US|work=The Wall Street Journal|url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/north-korea-suspended-from-olympics-11631130538|access-date=19 November 2021|issn=0099-9660}}

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: On 6 December 2021, White House Press Secretary, Jen Psaki, announced that the Biden administration would initiate a diplomatic boycott of the 2022 Winter Olympics and the 2022 Winter Paralympics. The diplomatic boycott would bar all US government officials from attending the games in an official capacity. The White House cited China's mistreatment of the Uyghur people as the reason for the boycott. The White House said it stopped short of a full boycott, because "it would not be fair to punish athletes who have trained for years".

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: On 27 December 2021, the Chinese foreign ministry said it has received visa applications for 18 US officials to attend the games.{{Cite news|title=China says 18 US officials have filed visa requests to visit Beijing Winter Olympics|url=https://www.australiannews.net/news/272040787/china-says-18-us-officials-have-filed-visa-requests-to-visit-beijing-winter-olympics|date=27 December 2021|access-date=4 January 2022}} The US said that the visa applications were consistent with its diplomatic boycott as the applicants would only be providing "consular and diplomatic security services" to its athletes.{{Cite news|title=Biden's diplomatic boycott stands despite asking to send 18 officials to Beijing Winter Olympics: US|url=https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3161250/bidens-diplomatic-boycott-stands-despite-asking-send-18|date=28 December 2021|access-date=4 January 2022}}

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: China's alleged use of coercive diplomacy against Australia has led to increased calls within Australia to boycott the 2022 Winter Olympics. In November 2020, Australian Senators Jacqui Lambie and Rex Patrick officially proposed a boycott, but their proposal was voted down.{{cite web|last1=Citowicki|first1=Philip|title=Continued Deterioration in Australia-China Relations Fuels Talk of Olympic Boycott|url=https://thediplomat.com/2020/11/continued-deterioration-in-australia-china-relations-fuels-talk-of-olympic-boycott/|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20201123073543/https://thediplomat.com/2020/11/continued-deterioration-in-australia-china-relations-fuels-talk-of-olympic-boycott/|archive-date=23 November 2020|access-date=24 November 2020|website=thediplomat.com|publisher=The Diplomat|date=20 November 2020}} Australia has decided that no Australian based politician or officials will be attending the games, and Canberra has also refused to sign the Olympic Truce for the 2022 Winter Olympics.{{cite news|title=Australia refuses to sign 'truce' for Beijing Olympics as it weighs up diplomatic boycott|url=https://theworldnews.net/au-news/australia-refuses-to-sign-truce-for-beijing-olympics-as-it-weighs-up-diplomatic-boycott|date=3 December 2021|access-date=7 February 2022}}

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: On 7 December 2021, Australian Prime Minister Scott Morrison stated that Australia would join with the United States in the diplomatic boycott of the 2022 games. He stated that it was "human rights abuses," referencing the ongoing genocide of Uyghur Muslims in China's Xinjiang region, as well as "many other issues that Australia has consistently raised". He went on to state that it was "no surprise" that Canberra would do this following consistent deterioration of relations between Canberra and Beijing. Morrison also stated that the decision was "in Australia's national interest," and that it is the "right thing to do."

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: Qi Fabao had been captured in June 2020 by Indian forces when he tried to mount an attack on Indian forces in the Galwan Valley, according to an investigative report by the Australian newspaper The Klaxon. According to the report, 38 Chinese troops drowned in the early stages of the 15–16 June face-off between Indian and Chinese forces while attempting to cross the Galwan River at Line of Actual Control in the dark. The Chinese government accepted four casualties.

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: The IOC has stated that the diplomatic boycotts are "a purely political decision for each government, which the IOC in its political neutrality fully respects."{{cite news | url=https://economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/sports/ioc-respects-us-diplomatic-boycott-of-beijing-olympics/articleshow/88140582.cms | title=IOC 'respects' US diplomatic boycott of Beijing Olympics | newspaper=The Economic Times }} It has also stated that the award of hosting the games does not signal agreement with the host country's political or social situation or its human rights standards. When prompted by Agence France-Presse, the IOC responded: "We've repeatedly said it: the IOC isn't responsible for the government. It only gives the rights and opportunity for the staging of the Olympic Games. That doesn't mean we agree with all the politics, all the social or human rights issues in the country. And it doesn't mean we approve of all the human rights violations of a person or people." This position has generated criticism, with Jules Boykoff accusing the IOC of hypocrisy by saying that it ignores its charter that promotes equality and anti-discrimination when it is convenient to do so and that the IOC has shown an "unfortunate propensity for turning away from human rights atrocities to make sure that the games go on."

During the men's downhill event in alpine skiing, German coach Christian Schweiger said the following, "the catering is extremely questionable. This shows a lack of focus on high-performance sport".{{cite news|last=O'Connor|first=Philip|date=6 February 2022|title=Alpine skiing-Cold food riles Germany coach, U.S. bring own pasta|url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/alpine-skiing-cold-food-riles-germany-coach-us-bring-own-pasta-2022-02-06/|work=[[Reuters]]|location=London, United Kingdom|access-date=11 February 2022}} Also, Russian Olympic Committee biathlete Valeria Vasnetsova posted on social media that she was served the same food for all three meals and posted "My stomach hurts, I'm very pale and I have huge black circles around my eyes". PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: On 9 December 2019, the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) banned Russia from all international sport for a period of four years, after the Russian government was found to have tampered with lab data that it provided to WADA in January 2019 as a condition of the Russian Anti-Doping Agency being reinstated. As a result of the ban, WADA will allow individually cleared Russian athletes to take part in the 2022 Winter Olympics under a neutral banner, as instigated at the 2018 Winter Olympics. The title of the neutral banner was yet to be determined; WADA Compliance Review Committee head Jonathan Taylor stated that the IOC would not be able to use "Olympic Athletes from Russia" (OAR) as it did in 2018, emphasizing that neutral athletes cannot be portrayed as representing a specific country.{{Cite news|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2019/dec/09/russia-banned-from-tokyo-olympics-and-football-world-cup|title=Russia banned from Tokyo Olympics and football World Cup|last=MacInnes|first=Paul|date=9 December 2019|work=The Guardian|access-date=9 December 2019|language=en-GB|issn=0261-3077|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191209155622/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2019/dec/09/russia-banned-from-tokyo-olympics-and-football-world-cup|archive-date=9 December 2019|url-status=live}}{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/50710598|title=Russia banned for four years to include 2020 Olympics and 2022 World Cup|work=BBC Sport|date=9 December 2019|access-date=9 December 2019|language=en-GB |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211171354/https://www.bbc.com/sport/olympics/50710598 |archive-date=11 December 2019 |url-status=live}}{{cite news |url=https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2019/12/13/olympics/wada-lawyer-defends-lack-blanket-ban-russia/ |title=WADA lawyer defends lack of blanket ban on Russia |date=13 December 2019 |access-date=17 December 2019 |agency=Associated Press |work=[[The Japan Times]] |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191214162048/https://www.japantimes.co.jp/sports/2019/12/13/olympics/wada-lawyer-defends-lack-blanket-ban-russia/#.Xfknqej7S00 |archive-date=14 December 2019 |url-status=live }}

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: Russia later filed an appeal to the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) against the WADA decision.{{Cite magazine|url=https://time.com/5756077/russia-olympic-ban-appeal/ |title=Russia Confirms It Will Appeal 4-Year Olympic Ban |date=27 December 2019 |magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191227213853/https://time.com/5756077/russia-olympic-ban-appeal/ |archive-date=27 December 2019}} The Court of Arbitration for Sport, on review of Russia's appeal of its case from WADA, ruled on 17 December 2020, to reduce the penalty that WADA had placed from four to two years. Instead of banning Russia from sporting events, the ruling allowed Russia to participate at the Olympics and other international events, but for a period of two years, the team cannot use the Russian name, flag, or anthem and must present themselves as "Neutral Athlete" or "Neutral Team". The ruling does allow for team uniforms to display "Russia" on the uniform as well as the use of the Russian flag colors within the uniform's design, although the name should be up to equal predominance as the "Neutral Athlete/Team" designation.{{cite news | url = https://apnews.com/article/russia-banned-name-flag-olympic-games-a8bd342806883f66152859701d5ae5d4 | title=  Russia can't use its name and flag at the next 2 Olympics | first = Graham | last = Dunbar |date = 17 December 2020 | access-date= 17 December 2020 | work = Associated Press }}

The ROC team would be represented by the flag of the Russian Olympic Committee.{{cite news |title=Olympics: Russia to compete under ROC acronym in Tokyo as part of doping sanctions |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/us-olympics-2020-russia/olympics-russia-to-compete-under-roc-acronym-in-tokyo-as-part-of-doping-sanctions-idUSKBN2AJ1UZ |access-date=20 February 2021 |work=Reuters |date=19 February 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210220020504/https://www.reuters.com/article/us-olympics-2020-russia/olympics-russia-to-compete-under-roc-acronym-in-tokyo-as-part-of-doping-sanctions-idUSKBN2AJ1UZ |archive-date=20 February 2021 |url-status=dead}} On 22 April 2021, the IOC approved a fragment of Pyotr Tchaikovsky's Piano Concerto No. 1 to be used in place of the Russian national anthem.{{cite web|title=Tchaikovsky Selection To Replace Banned Russian Anthem At Tokyo 2020 and Beijing 2022 Olympics|url=https://www.rferl.org/a/russia-olympics-anthem-tchaikovsky-doping-ban-tokyo-beijing/31217728.html|date=22 April 2021|website=RadioFreeEurope/RadioLiberty}}

On 24 February 2022, president Vladimir Putin commenced a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, resulting in further sporting sanctions against Russia.{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/opinions/2022/02/18/olympics-shows-what-happens-when-putin-transgressions-go-unchecked/ |title=The Olympics show what happens when Putin's transgressions go unchecked |date=2022-02-18 |author1=Max Boot |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |place=Washington, D.C. |issn=0190-8286 |oclc=1330888409}}{{cite web | url=https://www.espn.com/olympics/story/_/id/33368931/international-olympic-committee-urges-sports-bodies-cancel-events-russia-belarus | title=IOC pushes to cancel events in Russia, Belarus | date=25 February 2022 }} Many news outlets have alleged that China suggested to Russia not to conduct the latter's invasion on Ukraine before the conclusion of the Beijing Olympics.{{Cite web |title=China asked Russia not to invade Ukraine during the Olympics – DW – 03/03/2022 |url=https://www.dw.com/en/china-asked-russia-to-wait-for-olympics-to-end-before-invading-ukraine/a-60994583 |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=dw.com |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=China asked Russia to delay invasion until after Olympics, Western intel shows |url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/03/02/world/china-russia-ukraine-invasion-olympics-western-intel/index.html |access-date=2023-03-31 |website=CNN |date=3 March 2022 |language=en}}{{cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/03/02/us/politics/russia-ukraine-china.html | title=China Asked Russia to Delay Ukraine War Until After Olympics, U.S. Officials Say | work=The New York Times | date=2 March 2022 | last1=Wong | first1=Edward | last2=Barnes | first2=Julian E. }}

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: All attendees to the Games, including athletes, audience members, and media, are required to use the My2022 app purportedly for daily Covid monitoring. The cybersecurity group Citizen Lab, a research institute at the University of Toronto's Munk School of Global Affairs and Public Policy, warned that the My2022 app fails to provide encryption on many of its files, and has security weaknesses that leave users exposed to data breaches. The Citizen Lab disclosed the concerns about the app on 3 December 2021, giving the organizing 15 days to respond and 45 days to fix the issues.  A new iOS version of MY2022 was released on 6 January 2022, which failed to fix these problems, while adding a new "Green Health Code", feature that collects more medical data and also lacks SSL certificate validation making it vulnerable to attacks.{{cite web|url=https://globalnews.ca/news/8519133/olympic-my2022-app-vulnerabilities-toronto-reaearch-lab-finds/|title=Toronto lab finds security vulnerabilities, censorship framework in Olympic MY2022 app | Globalnews.ca|website=Global News}}

Olympic Halfpipe Flips, Twists Explained|url=https://www.nbcnewyork.com/news/sports/beijing-winter-olympics/what-is-triple-cork-in-snowboarding-olympic-halfpipe-flips-twists-explained/3542695/|access-date=2022-02-12|website=NBC New York|date=9 February 2022 |language=en-US}}

Block: In the men's 500 metres speed skating event, a false start was called in the last two heats, one of which included current World Cup champion Laurent Dubreuil. This was questioned by 1992 Winter Olympics Champion Bart Veldkamp, who called it "very suspicious".{{cite web|url=https://sporza.be/nl/2022/02/12/jury-veroorzaakt-ophef-met-valse-start-voor-canadese-topfavoriet-heel-verdacht~1644666526044/|title=Jury veroorzaakt ophef met "valse start" voor Canadese topfavoriet: "Heel verdacht"|trans-title=Jury causes controversy with "false start" for Canadian top favorite: "Very suspicious"|language=Dutch|date=12 February 2022|website=www.sporza.be|publisher=[[Sporza]]|access-date=12 February 2022}} According to Yetta Claytone of the Taylor Daily Press, due to the false start, Dubreuil had to be more cautious on his start, and his reaction time was slower than the initial start.{{cite news|last=Claytone|first=Yetta|date=12 February 2022|title=The jury makes a fuss with 'false start' for Canadian top candidates: 'Extremely fishy' Winter Games|url=https://www.taylordailypress.net/the-jury-makes-a-fuss-with-false-start-for-canadian-top-candidates-extremely-fishy-winter-games/|work=[[Taylor Daily Press]]|location=Taylor, Texas, United States|access-date=12 February 2022}} According to Sportnieuws.nl, a false start would have disrupted the athletes' concentration, and also used up energy.{{cite web|url=https://sportnieuws.nl/schaatsen/bart-veldkamp-vertrouwt-500-m-zege-tingyu-gao-niet-2-hele-twijfelachtige-valse-starts/|trans-title=Bart Veldkamp does not trust Tingyu Gao 500 m victory: '2 very doubtful false starts'|title=Bart Veldkamp vertrouwt 500 m-zege Tingyu Gao niet: '2 hele twijfelachtige valse starts'|language=Dutch|date=12 February
