possible to overcome and that it shouldn't make a difference".{{cite web|title=Canadian speedskater Laurent Dubreuil edged off Olympic 500-metre podium in fourth|url=https://ca.sports.yahoo.com/news/canadian-speedskater-laurent-dubreuil-edged-135722451.html|access-date=2022-02-13|website=ca.sports.yahoo.com|language=en-CA}}

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: The medal ceremony for the figure skating team event, originally scheduled for Tuesday, 8 February, was delayed over what International Olympic Committee (IOC) spokesperson Mark Adams described as a situation that required "legal consultation" with the International Skating Union.{{Cite web|date=9 February 2022|title=Olympic medals in team figure skating delayed by legal issue|url=https://apnews.com/article/winter-olympics-figure-skating-sports-international-olympic-committee-court-of-arbitration-for-sport-c49077705737be8a7d41a2847c2f355b|access-date=9 February 2022|website=[[The Associated Press|AP News]]|language=en}} Several media outlets reported on Wednesday that the issue was over a positive test, held in December 2021, for trimetazidine by the ROC's Kamila Valieva,{{Cite news|last1=Tétrault-Farber|first1=Gabrielle|last2=Axon|first2=Iain|last3=Grohmann|first3=Karolos|date=9 February 2022|title=Figure skating-Russian media say teen star tested positive for banned drug|language=en|work=[[Reuters]]|url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/figure-skating-medals-ceremony-delayed-over-legal-consultation-2022-02-09/|access-date=9 February 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/beijing/2022/02/09/olympic-figure-skating-team-medals-delayed-russian-drug-test/6717526001/|title=Positive drug test by Russian Kamila Valieva has forced a delay of Olympic team medals ceremony|first=Christine|last=Brennan|author-link=Christine Brennan|website=[[USA Today]]|date=9 February 2022}} which was officially confirmed on February 11. The results are pending investigation.{{Cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/winter-olympics/60329120|title=Valieva failed drugs test confirmed|date=11 February 2022|website=BBC Sport|access-date=15 February 2022}} The Russian Anti-Doping Agency (RUSADA), previously under suspension from the World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA) since 2015{{cite news |last=Faloyin |first=Dipo |title=WADA Suspends Russia's Anti-Doping Agency |date=19 November 2015 |work=[[Newsweek]] |url=http://europe.newsweek.com/wada-suspends-russias-anti-doping-agency-non-compliance-396283?rm=eu |access-date=14 February 2022}} for its years of serving solely to hide the positive doping results of Russian athletes (re-instated in September 2018),"Wada lifts Russia's three-year doping suspension and faces its biggest crisis". By Sean Ingle. The Guardian. Sept 20, 2018. [https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2018/sep/20/wada-crisis-lifts-russia-suspension-anti-doping]{{cite news |first=Bonnie D. |last=Ford |title=Takeaways from McLaren Report? Confusion, corruption, cynicism |date=18 July 2016 |work=[[ESPN]] |url = http://espn.go.com/olympics/story/_/id/17100024/takeaways-mclaren-report-confusion-corruption-cynicism |access-date=13 February 2022}}{{Cite news |first=Maggie |last=Hendricks |title=The damning McLaren Report on Russian Olympic doping, explained |date=18 July 2016 |work=[[USA Today]] |url=http://ftw.usatoday.com/2016/07/the-damning-mclaren-report-on-russian-olympic-doping-explained |access-date=13 February 2022}} cleared Valieva on February 9, a day after the December test results were released, two months after the test. The IOC, WADA, and International Skating Union (ISU) are appealing RUSADA's decision.{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/02/10/sport/kamila-valieva-roc-drugs-test-olympics-spt-intl-hnk/index.html|title=Russian anti-doping agency allowed Kamila Valieva to compete in Olympics despite failed drug test|website=Cnn.com|date=11 February 2022 |access-date=15 February 2022}}

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: On February 14, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled that Valieva should be allowed to compete in the women's single event, deciding that preventing her from competing "would cause her irreparable harm in the circumstances", though her gold medal in the team event was still under consideration. The favorable decision from the court was made in part due to her age, as minor athletes are subject to different rules than adult athletes.{{Cite web|date=2022-02-14|title=Russian skater Kamila Valieva cleared to compete at Olympics|url=https://apnews.com/article/winter-olympics-kamila-valieva-doping-decision-0dd063b5092681697525b69cd0c7212d|access-date=2022-02-14|website=Apnews.com|language=en}}{{cite web|url=https://www.tas-cas.org/fileadmin/user_upload/CAS_Ad_Hoc_Media_Release_Beijing_8.pdf|title=THE CAS AD HOC DIVISION DECLINES TO IMPOSE A PROVISIONAL SUSPENSION ON THE RUSSIAN FIGURE SKATER KAMILA VALIEVA|website=Tas-cas.org|access-date=2022-02-15}} The IOC announced that the medal ceremony would not take place until the investigation is over and there is a concrete decision whether to strip Russia of their medals.{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/ioc/news/ioc-eb-decides-no-medal-ceremonies-following-cas-decision-on-the-case-of-roc-skater|title=IOC EB decides no medal ceremonies following CAS decision on the case of ROC skater|website=Olympics.com|access-date=2022-02-15}}

PageTitle: Concerns and controversies at the 2022 Winter Olympics
Block: By 9 March 2022, Travis Tygart of the USADA reported that Valieva had not requested that her "B" sample be tested, apparently accepting the results of initial testing and relying on her explanation that the banned substance TMZ belonged to her grandfather and only accidentally contaminated or became mixed into her own use of allowed nutrients and supplements. Tygart further stated that as a minor Valieva could still be either fully exculpated or given a warning concerning her testing positive depending on the extent of findings in the on-going RUSADA investigation of doping. According to Tygart, an adverse finding against her as a first offense could still be assessed as a two-year suspension, which is half of the suspension time which could be assessed for adults.{{cite AV media |date=8 March 2022 |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q52SeSRjB1E |title=As The Blade Turns: Interview with Travis Tygart (USADA, Kamila Valieva Doping, Russian Doping) |publisher=TheSkatingLesson |via=[[YouTube]] |access-date=28 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220813211646/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Q52SeSRjB1E |archive-date=13 August 2022 |url-status=live}}

Block: The U.S. speedskater Joey Mantia alleged that the South Korean speedskater Lee Seung-hoon made contact by pulling his arm back, costing him the bronze medal during the Mass Start final. Mantia lost by a 0.002-second margin.{{cite web | url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/beijing/2022/02/19/joey-mantia-photo-finish-beijing-olympics/6859615001/ | title='Cheated a little bit': Photo finish in wild men's speedskating race leaves Joey Mantia off podium | website=[[USA Today]] }}{{cite web | url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/sports/more-sports/cheated-a-little-bit-photo-finish-in-wild-men-s-speedskating-race-leaves-joey-mantia-off-podium/ar-AAU43Yp | title='Cheated a little bit': Photo finish in wild men's speedskating race leaves Joey Mantia off podium | website=[[MSN]] }}{{cite web | url=https://sports.yahoo.com/american-speed-skater-loses-medal-by-thousandth-of-a-second-101719003.html | title=American speed skater loses medal by thousandth of a second | date=19 February 2022 }}{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/olympics/2022/02/19/joey-mantia-mass-start-speedskating-beijing-olympics/ |title=In his final Olympic event, Joey Mantia missed a medal — by 0.002 seconds |date=2022-02-22 |orig-date=2022-02-19 |author1=Roman Stubbs |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |place=Washington, D.C. |issn=0190-8286 |oclc=1330888409}}{{WaPoCheckDates}} According to Mantia, he felt contact and told his coach "He got me" after the race. Mantia recalled "Coming up on him, I thought my blade was in front of his, and then he put his back in front of mine. I don't know if there was contact ... it felt like maybe a little bit, maybe not on purpose, but it happens." When asked if he made the contact with Mantia, Lee said he could not remember since he was flustered during the final moment at the finish line. Mantia and his coaches watched the replay several times, and protested that he had been pulled back at the finish line. However, the team did not expect any changes to the result because the Mass Final is a new event with minimal precedent for rules.{{cite web | url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/2022/02/19/sports/panel-denies-us-figure-skaters-appeal-get-olympic-team-silver-medals/ | title=Panel denies US figure skaters' appeal to get Olympic team silver medals - the Boston Globe | website=[[The Boston Globe]] }} The United States team lodged a challenge, but Lee was awarded with the bronze medal.

Block: Cases of COVID-19 at the 2022 Winter Olympics and the 2022 Winter Paralympics in Beijing, China, is a cluster of SARS-CoV-2 infections within the COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China that began in the Beijing 2022 Olympic Village in January 2022, prior to the Opening Ceremony of the games on 4 February 2022.

PageTitle: COVID-19 cases at the 2022 Winter Olympics and 2022 Winter Paralympics
Block: There were 437 total coronavirus cases detected and reported by the Beijing Organizing Committee for the 2022 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games since 23 January 2022.{{Cite web|last=Fenno|first=Nathan|date=2022-02-20|title=How effective was China at stopping coronavirus at Olympics? - Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/olympics/story/2022-02-19/china-closed-loop-beijing-olympics-coronavirus|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220220235336/https://www.latimes.com/sports/olympics/story/2022-02-19/china-closed-loop-beijing-olympics-coronavirus|archive-date=2022-02-20|access-date=2022-02-23|website=Los Angeles Times}} All cases at the 2022 Olympics are counted towards China's COVID case count rather than the home country of the person.

PageTitle: COVID-19 cases at the 2022 Winter Olympics and 2022 Winter Paralympics
Block: There were 26 cases in the time period after the 2022 Winter Olympics, which includes the 2022 Winter Paralympics.{{Cite news|last=Pavitt|first=Michael|date=14 March 2022|title=Final figures reveal that Beijing 2022 conducted over 2.5 million COVID-19 tests on participants at Olympics and Paralympics|work=[[Inside the Games|InsideTheGames.biz]]|url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1120547/beijing-2022-25-million-covid-19-tests|access-date=14 March 2022}} In total, more than 2.5 million tests for COVID-19 were conducted.

Block: On 31 July 2015, Beijing was selected as the host city of the 2022 Winter Olympics, officially the XXIV Olympic Winter Games, during the 128th IOC Session in Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia.{{cite web|date=31 July 2015|title=Beijing to host 2022 Winter Olympics and Paralympics|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/winter-olympics/33730477|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151210203921/https://www.bbc.com/sport/winter-olympics/33730477|archive-date=10 December 2015|access-date=31 July 2015|work=BBC Sport}} It was elected over Almaty. The games were the second Olympic Games to be held in China following Beijing 2008 (Summer). As a result, Beijing will also be the first city to host both the Summer and the Winter Games for the Olympics and Paralympics.

Block: During the 2020 Tokyo Summer Olympics, there were 464 COVID-19 cases linked to the games.{{Cite web|last=Fenno|first=Nathan|date=2022-02-20|title=How effective was China at stopping coronavirus at Olympics? - Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/olympics/story/2022-02-19/china-closed-loop-beijing-olympics-coronavirus|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220220235336/https://www.latimes.com/sports/olympics/story/2022-02-19/china-closed-loop-beijing-olympics-coronavirus|archive-date=2022-02-20|access-date=2022-02-23|website=Los Angeles Times}} Despite the strict COVID-19 containment efforts including bubbles{{Cite web|title=Winter Olympics in Beijing draws to a close: Marred by strict COVID-19 rules, fake snow and Kamila Valieva's doping scandal|url=https://news.sky.com/story/winter-olympics-in-beijing-draws-to-a-close-marred-by-strict-covid-19-rules-fake-snow-and-kamila-valievas-doping-scandal-12547333|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220220183939/https://news.sky.com/story/winter-olympics-in-beijing-draws-to-a-close-marred-by-strict-covid-19-rules-fake-snow-and-kamila-valievas-doping-scandal-12547333|archive-date=2022-02-20|access-date=2022-02-23|website=Sky News|language=en}} and claims of being the safest sporting event,{{Cite news|last=Kilgore|first=Adam|date=2022-02-18|title=The Beijing Olympics' closed loop eliminated covid, at a price - The Washington Post|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/olympics/2022/02/18/beijing-olympics-closed-loop/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220218161537/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/olympics/2022/02/18/beijing-olympics-closed-loop/|archive-date=2022-02-18|access-date=2022-02-23}} the Beijing Winter Olympics reported only 27 fewer cases than the similar scale event during the 2020 Tokyo Summer Olympics, which had less stringent COVID-19 containment measures.

The 2022 Winter Olympics in Beijing was televised by a number of broadcasters throughout the world. As with previous years, Olympic Broadcasting Services produced the world feed provided to local broadcasters for use in their coverage. In most regions, broadcast rights to the 2022 and 2024 Olympics were packaged together, but some broadcasters obtained rights to further games as well.

In some countries, broadcast rights to the 2022 Winter Olympics are already agreed upon through existing long-term deals. In France and the United Kingdom, these are the first Games where Eurosport will be the main rightsholder; the BBC will sub-license a limited amount of coverage on free-to-air television, as part of a deal in which the BBC sold the pay-TV rights to the 2018 and 2020 Games to Eurosport.{{cite news|title=BBC dealt another blow after losing control of TV rights for Olympics|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2015/jun/29/bbc-loses-control-olympic-tv-rights-discovery-eurosport|website=The Guardian|date=29 June 2015 |access-date=30 June 2015 |last1=Gibson |first1=Owen }}{{cite news|title=Olympics coverage to remain on BBC after Discovery deal|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2016/feb/02/olympics-bbc-discovery-deal|website=The Guardian|date=2 February 2016 |access-date=7 June 2016 |last1=Gibson |first1=Owen }}

In China, domestic rights to these Games are owned by China Central Television (CCTV), with live rights being sublicensed by China Mobile's Migu streaming service.{{cite news|title=中国移动咪咕成中央广播电视总台奥运会、欧洲杯、冬奥会、世界杯赛事转播顶级合作伙伴|url=http://sports.xinhuanet.com/c/2020-12/09/c_1126841567.htm|access-date=17 July 2021|work=sports.news.cn|date=9 December 2020|language=zh}}

In the United States, these Games will once again be broadcast by NBCUniversal properties, as part of its US$7.75 billion contract{{cite web|date=7 December 2017|title=Fewer Russians Could Be a Windfall for U.S. Olympic Business|url=https://mobile.nytimes.com/2017/12/07/sports/olympics/russia-olympics-us-business.html|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180205184807/https://mobile.nytimes.com/2017/12/07/sports/olympics/russia-olympics-us-business.html|archive-date=5 February 2018|access-date=5 February 2018|work=[[The New York Times]]}} to air the Olympics through 2032.{{cite news|date=7 May 2014|title=Olympics on NBC through 2032|newspaper=[[USA Today]]|publisher=[[Gannett Company]]|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/2014/05/07/nbc-olympics-broadcast-rights-2032/8805989/|url-status=live|access-date=18 May 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190501023722/https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/olympics/2014/05/07/nbc-olympics-broadcast-rights-2032/8805989/|archive-date=1 May 2019}}

2022 Winter Olympics marketing was a long running campaign that began since Beijing won its bid to host the games in 2015.
[[File:B-5425@PEK (20200905172542).jpg|thumb|An Air China Boeing 737-800 with 2022 Winter Olympics special livery, featuring the emblems and mascots]]

The official emblem "Winter Dream" () was unveiled on 15 December 2017 at the Beijing National Aquatics Center. The emblem is a stylized rendition of the character "冬" (Winter) inspired by winter snow, with a ribbon motif. The top is meant to resemble a skier and the bottom is meant to resemble a skater. The emblem also features the Olympic colors (except black) and the Chinese flag colors. The emblem was designed by Lin Cunzhen who also created the  Nanjing 2014 logo.{{cite news|url=http://olympics.nbcsports.com/2017/12/15/beijing-2022-winter-olympic-logo/|title=Beijing 2022 Winter Olympic logo unveiled|date=15 December 2017|agency=NBC Sports |work=nbcsports.com|accessdate=17 December 2017|first=Nick|last=Zaccardi}}

The Games' promotional slogan is Joyful Rendezvous Upon Pure Ice and Snow (), which was used for the candidature process for Beijing to bid for the 2022 Games. On September 17, 2021 the Beijing 2022 announce the slogan of Olympic Winter Games  "Together for a Shared Future!" ().{{Cite web|date=2021-09-17|title=Beijing 2022 reveals official motto: "Together for a Shared Future" - Olympic News|url=https://olympics.com/ioc/news/beijing-2022-reveals-official-motto-together-for-a-shared-future|access-date=2021-10-07|website=International Olympic Committee|language=en}} A song with the same name, "Together for a Shared Future" was sung in two versions: one by Jackson Yee, the other by William Chan and Tia Ray; to promote the slogan of the Winter Olympics and Paralympics.{{Cite web|title=易烊千玺以歌助威北京冬奥，单曲《一起向未来》上线QQ音乐|url=https://finance.ifeng.com/c/89hQxOahbn7|url-status=live|access-date=2021-10-07|website=凤凰网|language=Chinese|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211007172204/https://finance.ifeng.com/c/89hQxOahbn7 |archive-date=2021-10-07 }}

Medalists at the 2022 Winter Olympics

The 2022 Winter Olympics opening ceremony was held at Beijing National Stadium, China on 4 February 2022. As mandated by the Olympic Charter, the proceedings are expected to combine the formal and ceremonial opening of this international sporting event, including welcoming speeches, hoisting of the flags and the parade of athletes, with an artistic spectacle to showcase the host nation's winter culture and modern history.{{Cite web|date=2021-09-30|title=Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games Beijing 2022 – Updates on Spectators, Vaccination and COVID-19 Countermeasures|url=https://olympics.com/ioc/news/olympic-and-paralympic-winter-games-beijing-2022-updates-on-spectators-vaccination-and-covid-19-countermeasures|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211010144650/https://olympics.com/ioc/news/olympic-and-paralympic-winter-games-beijing-2022-updates-on-spectators-vaccination-and-covid-19-countermeasures|archive-date=10 October 2021|access-date=2021-10-10|website=International Olympic Committee}} The Games were officially opened by Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Chinese Communist Party and president of the People's Republic of China.{{Cite web|date=2021-11-23|title=How do the Olympic Games opening and closing ceremonies take place|url=https://olympics.com/ioc/faq/games-ceremonies-and-protocol/how-do-the-olympic-games-opening-and-closing-ceremonies-take-place|access-date=2021-12-08|website=International Olympic Committee|language=en|archive-date=19 November 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211119013958/https://olympics.com/ioc/faq/games-ceremonies-and-protocol/how-do-the-olympic-games-opening-and-closing-ceremonies-take-place|url-status=live}}

The opening ceremony was directed by film director and producer Zhang Yimou, who has previously directed the opening and closing ceremonies of the 2008 Summer Olympics, which was China's first time hosting the Olympics.{{cite news|title=Chinese director Zhang Yimou to oversee opening ceremony of 2022 Winter Olympics|url=https://www.thestandard.com.hk/breaking-news/section/3/185651/Chinese-director-Zhang-Yimou-to-oversee-opening-ceremony-of-2022-Winter-Olympics%C2%A0|access-date=19 January 2022|agency=Reuters|publisher=The Standard|date=8 January 2022|archive-date=19 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220119224931/https://www.thestandard.com.hk/breaking-news/section/3/185651/Chinese-director-Zhang-Yimou-to-oversee-opening-ceremony-of-2022-Winter-Olympics%C2%A0|url-status=live }}{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2022/feb/04/beijing-2022-winter-olympics-opening-ceremony-live|title=Beijing 2022: Winter Olympics opening ceremony – live!|date=4 February 2022|work=Guardian|access-date=4 February 2022|archive-date=4 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220204111733/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/live/2022/feb/04/beijing-2022-winter-olympics-opening-ceremony-live|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.yahoo.com/video/us-applies-visas-18-officials-181029193.html|title=US applies for visas for 18 officials to attend Beijing Winter Olympics amid diplomatic boycott|date=27 December https://nypost.com/2021/12/27/us-says-diplomats-going-to-beijing-to-help-athletes-after-china-blasts-boycott/|title = US says diplomats going to Beijing to help athletes after China blasts boycott 'farce'|date = 27 December 2021|access-date = 5 February 2022|archive-date = 30 December 2021|archive-url = stadium.jpg|thumb|Beijing National Stadium]]

The world's largest LED screen ( and uses 40,000 LED modules) was unveiled at the opening ceremony.{{cite news|last1=Pino|first1=Nick|title=China built the 'world's largest' LED screen for the 2022 Winter Olympics Opening Ceremony|url=https://www.techradar.com/news/china-built-the-worlds-largest-led-screen-for-the-2022-winter-olympics-opening-ceremony|access-date=5 February 2022|publisher=TechRadar|date=5 February 2022|archive-date=5 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205022221/https://www.techradar.com/news/china-built-the-worlds-largest-led-screen-for-the-2022-winter-olympics-opening-ceremony|url-status=live }}
The ceremony was also marked by diplomatic boycotts among other concerns and controversies.
As stated by Zhang Yimou, in an Olympic first, all of the segments along with the International Olympic Committee protocols, were merged into one integrated programme in the opening ceremony.

The final stage in preparations for the event and performance stages at the Bird's Nest were completed in October.{{cite news|last1=Burke|first1=Patrick|title=Full rehearsal held for Opening Ceremony of Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics|url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1118166/beijing-2022-opening-ceremony-rehearsal|access-date=28 January 2022|agency=Inside the games|date=23 January 2022|archive-date=23 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220123124438/https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1118166/beijing-2022-opening-ceremony-rehearsal|url-status=live }} A full-scale dress rehearsal was held on 22 January 2022, with approximately 4000 participants featuring in it.

A 30-minute pre-show performance kicked off at 19:25, featuring square dancers aged from five to over 70 years old.{{cite news|title=Olympic opening ceremony held in Beijing|url=https://www.macaubusiness.com/olympic-opening-ceremony-held-in-beijing/|access-date=5 February 2022|agency=Macao Business|date=5 February 2022}} Apart from the live performances, people from other Chinese cities joined the pre-show performances through video recording. The pre-show performance was performed primarily by residents of Beijing and Hebei Province, showcasing the passion of the Chinese people in welcoming the Olympic Winter Games.{{cite news|title=Splendid opening ceremony raises curtain on Games|url=https://www.khmertimeskh.com/501019513/splendid-opening-ceremony-raises-curtain-on-games/|access-date=5 February 2022|agency=Khmer Times|date=5 February 2022}}

At 20:00, the words "" (guònián hǎo,  "Happy New Year") and "Happy Chinese New Year" appeared on the stage after the 30-minute long performances, symbolizing China's hospitality and celebrations of the traditional Chinese festival.

Chinese paramount leader Xi Jinping, Chinese First Lady Peng Liyuan, IOC President Thomas Bach, international dignitaries and various Chinese government officials arrived at the stadium before the official start of the ceremony, receiving huge cheers and welcome from the crowds and the performers from the pre-show performances.{{cite news|last1=Pavitt|first1=Michael|title=Beijing 2022 Olympic Games: Opening Ceremony|url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1118778/beijing-2022-opening-ceremony-live-blog|access-date=5 February 2022|agency=Inside the games|date=5 February 2022}}

The ceremony began with a 24-second countdown, which represented the 24th Winter Olympics as well as the 24 solar terms in the Chinese calendar,{{cite news|last1=Koreen|first1=Mike|title=Politics, COVID-19 front and centre during Beijing Olympics Opening Ceremony|url=https://www.sportsnet.ca/olympics/article/olympic-cauldron-lit-officially-opening-beijing-winter-olympics/|access-date=5 February 2022|agency=Sports net|date=5 February 2022|archive-date=4 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220204143519/https://www.sportsnet.ca/olympics/article/olympic-cauldron-lit-officially-opening-beijing-winter-olympics/|url-status=live }} where Lichun (ecliptic longitude 315°), Feb 4, is generally regarded as the "Beginning of spring". After the countdown, dancers carried tall and flexible glowing green stalks, showing the lifecycle of the dandelion, which eventually turned white and floated up into the sky as the seeds dispersed,{{cite news|last1=Belam|first1=Martin|title=Winter Olympics: 11 key moments from Beijing 2022 opening ceremony|url=https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2022/feb/04/beijing-2022-winter-olympics-opening-ceremony-11-key-moments|access-date=5 February 2022|agency=The Guardian|date=5 February 2022|archive-date=4 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220204233841/https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2022/feb/04/beijing-2022-winter-olympics-opening-ceremony-11-key-moments|url-status=live }} followed by fireworks displaying the words "" (lìchūn,  "the beginning of spring") and "Spring", celebrating the beginning of spring.{{cite web|language=zh|url=http://politics.people.com.cn/BIG5/n1/2022/0205/c1024-32345535.html|title=第二十四屆冬季奧林匹克運動會在北京隆重開幕|date=2022-02-05|publisher=www.people.com.cn}} At the beginning of the ceremony, a film about Dundbulag rock carvings from Altay in the Altay Prefecture was shown. Skiing is likely to originate from Altay per the 2015 Altay Declaration made by scholars from 18 countries.{{cite web|title=The origins of skiing are indigenous and 10,000 years old|url=https://natives-outdoors.com/temoajournal/2020/2/17/the-origins-of-skiing-are-indigenous-and-10000-years-old|website=NativesOutdoors|date=17 February 2020 |quote=[[Great Big Story]]|access-date=5 February 2022|archive-date=5 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205210614/https://natives-outdoors.com/temoajournal/2020/2/17/the-origins-of-skiing-are-indigenous-and-10000-years-old|url-status=live }}{{cite news|last1=Ye|first1=Liyue|title=The World's First Huge Chinese Calligraphy Written Through Skiing|url=https://finance.yahoo.com/news/worlds-first-huge-chinese-calligraphy-134500958.html|agency=Tsingtao Brewery Co. Ltd.|publisher=ACCESSWIRE|date=Apr 20, 2021|access-date=5 February 2022|archive-date=5 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205223952/https://finance.yahoo.com/news/worlds-first-huge-chinese-calligraphy-134500958.html|url-status=live }}
Chinese President Xi Jinping and IOC President Thomas Bach were then introduced by the MCs, receiving warm welcome from the crowds again.

Zhu De'en, a trumpeter, played a patriotic Chinese song "My People, My Country". Twelve children lifted the national flag of China and entered the stadium, symbolizing the legacy of Beijing 2008 opening ceremony. They then passed the national flag to a line of representatives from different strata of society and 56 ethnic groups of China, symbolizing national unity and the deep relationships between the national flag and the citizens. The representatives then handed over the flag to 8 PLAGF Honor Guard soldiers, who then unfurled and raised the flag while the crowd sang the Chinese national anthem.

The Olympic Rings performance began with the giant LED screens showing a drop of ink that had fallen from the sky, turning into seething, rolling waves of the Yellow River, from which an ice cube crystallizes. 24 "laser beams" sequentially "carve" the names of cities and countries of 23 previous Winter Olympics in Chinese and English on this cube. The 24th was shown when the rays merged into a single beam, which "cut out" "2022 BEIJING CHINA". Six hockey players then entered the stadium and swung at a massive LED hockey puck. It flew into the cube, slowly fracturing it as the five ice Olympic rings rose from behind. Next, a Chinese ice door opened behind them, and athletes began to enter the parade of nations.{{Cite web|date=2022-02-04|title=Uyghur athlete lights Olympic Cauldron as Beijing 2022 officially opens|url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1118798/beijing-2022-opening-ceremony|access-date=2022-02-04|website=Inside the Games}}

Following the formation of the ice Olympic rings, greetings appeared in the stadium in many languages of the world. Per tradition, the national team of Greece, the country of origin of Olympics marched first. The country that will host the next Winter Olympics, Italy, marched before the host nation, China, which entered last. The patriotic song "Ode to the Motherland" was played when China entered the stadium. Other teams, in the same practice of the opening ceremony of the 2008 Summer Olympics, entered in a collation method based on their countries names as written in Simplified Chinese characters and is similar to that used in Chinese dictionaries. The names were sorted by the number of strokes in the first character of the name, then by the stroke order of the character (in the stroke count method order), then the number of strokes and stroke order of the second character, then next character and so on.{{Cite news|last1=Mather|first1=Victor|last2=Buckley|first2=Chris|date=4 February 2022|title=The Chinese language determines the order of the Parade of Nations.|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/02/04/sports/opening-ceremony-order-of-countries.html|access-date=4 February 2022|issn=0362-4331}} In front of each country's delegation, a Chinese representative carried a snowflake-shaped sign with the name of the delegation in both English and Chinese. After the parade, all such "snowflakes" of the participating delegations formed a large "snowflake" to symbolise the world coming together.

Cai Qi, President of the Beijing 2022 organizing committee delivered a speech to thank and welcome the athletes, offering words of peace and unity.{{cite news|last1=Winsor|first1=Morgan|last2=Alfonseca|first2=Kiara|title=2022 Winter Olympics opening ceremony: Best moments from the event|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/live-updates/beijing-olympics-opening-ceremony/?id=82644432|access-date=5 February 2022|agency=ABC News|date=5 February 2022|archive-date=5 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205012346/https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/live-updates/beijing-olympics-opening-ceremony/?id=82644432|url-status=live }} IOC President Thomas Bach then gave his speech in which he thanked China for being gracious hosts and also extended gratitude to those on the doctors and nurses combating the global COVID-19 pandemic. Bach urged world leaders to "give peace a chance" amid the traditional Olympic truce and instructed athletes to "show how the world would look like, if we all respect the same rules and each other".{{Cite news|title=2022 Winter Olympics officially begin|language=en-GB|work=BBC Sport|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/winter-olympics/60242407|access-date=2022-02-04}} He also called for the end of various types of discrimination, especially against Asians worldwide.
On IOC President Thomas Bach's invitation, Chinese President Xi Jinping declared the 2022 Winter Olympics in Beijing officially open.
Fireworks then shined the sky, forming the shape of a "Welcome Pine", one of the symbols of the Huangshan, symbolizing China's warm welcome to guests from all over the world.

The performance began by a group of young people consisted of local and foreign university students, walking on the stage with the Chinese song "Let the World be Filled with Love" (, Ràng shìjiè chōngmǎn ài) sung in the background. After they walked past the stage, the slogan "Together for a shared future" (, Yīqǐ xiàng wèilái) in both English and Chinese appeared. Later, a group of ice skaters on the LED floor, carving out paths for them to follow, all to the theme of John Lennon's "Imagine" cover song{{Cite web|date=2022-02-04|title=WATCH: China Pays Tribute to John Lennon at Opening Ceremony of Beijing Winter Olympics 2022|url=https://www.essentiallysports.com/beijing-winter-olympics-2022-us-sports-news-watch-china-pays-tribute-to-john-lennon-at-opening-ceremony-of-beijing-winter-olympics-2022/|access-date=2022-02-16|website=EssentiallySports}} The Olympic motto "Faster, Higher, Stronger - Together" () also in both English and Chinese then appeared.
The Olympic Flag entered into the stadium. The flag bearers were:

The Olympic Anthem was sung in Greek by the Malanhua'er Children's Choir, a choir of 44 children from the mountains of Fuping County, Baoding, Hebei Province.{{cite news|title=New Winter Olympics · Heart Moved｜Children from mountains sing the Olympics hymn, Zhang Yimou moved 新冬奥·心感动｜大山里的娃娃冬奥唱响五环会歌，小小红脸蛋感动张艺谋|url=http://wap.xinmin.cn/content/32109029.html|access-date=5 February 2022|agency=Xinmin evening news (新民晚报)|date=5 February 2022}}{{cite web|url=https://www.abc.net.au/news/2022-02-04/winter-olympics-opening-ceremony-live-blog/100805728|title=Winter Olympics opening ceremony: Beijing 2022 Games are officially open after stirring ceremony at the Bird's Nest|date=2022-02-05|publisher=www.abc.net.au}}

Cross-country skier Wang Qiang and snowboard halfpipe athlete Liu Jiayu represented the athletes sworn the Olympic oath, while aerials judge Tao Yongchun and head of the Chinese coaching team in snowboard parallel giant slalom Ji Xiao'ou represented judges and coaches, respectively.

After the Olympic vows, a short film "Champions of Tomorrow" was shown on the screen of the stadium, showing toddlers taking their first steps in winter sports, set to the rendition of Chinese nursery rhyme Two Tigers. Although the toddlers fell over and over again, they did not lose heart and persisted.

In the performance, hundreds of children wandered around the center stage singing the theme song of the ceremony titled “Snowflake”. The LED floor beneath them used large-scale motion capture to illuminate glows of snowflakes and stars under their feet.  The children played happily, holding dove lamps and lanterns, leaving trails of glittering snowflakes as they went. As the song and dance came to a close, the children surrounded a massive snowflake in a heart-shaped formation while singing. The large snowflake consisted of 91 snowflake-shaped placards used for each participating country during the "Parade of Nations".{{cite news|last1=Molski|first1=Max|title=Children Star in 'Snowflake' Performance at Winter Olympics Opening Ceremony|url=https://www.nbcconnecticut.com/news/sports/beijing-winter-olympics/children-star-in-snowflake-performance-at-winter-olympics-opening-ceremony/2709933/|access-date=5 February 2022|publisher=NBC|date=4 February 2022|archive-date=4 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220204134143/https://www.nbcconnecticut.com/news/sports/beijing-winter-olympics/children-star-in-snowflake-performance-at-winter-olympics-opening-ceremony/2709933/|url-status=live }} The snowflake theme ran through the entire ceremony representing solidarity and prosperity.

At 22:10, the Olympic Flame from Olympia reached the stadium. After the Olympic anthem, it was passed around the stadium by five athletes born in the 1950s (Zhao Weichang), 1960s (Li Yan), 1970s (Yang Yang (A)), 1980s (Su Bingtian) and 1990s (Zhou Yang). The final torch-runners were two athletes born in the 2000s: Skier Dinigeer Yilamujiang and Nordic mixed skier Zhao Jiawen, who fitted the torch carrying Olympic flame in the center of the large "snowflake" engraved with the names of the 91 countries competing. For the first time in Olympic history the passing torch itself formed the main flame of the Olympic cauldron, known as a "microflame" (, Wéi huǒ). Director Zhang Yimou stated that the tiny flame symbolised environmental sustainability and set the standards for a "carbon-neutral" game.{{cite news|last1=Lau|first1=Jack|title=Tiny Olympic flame mocked, but director Zhang Yimou says it 'sets new standards' for 'carbon-neutral' Beijing Games|url=https://www.scmp.com/sport/china/article/3165949/tiny-olympic-flame-mocked-director-zhang-yimou-says-it-sets-new|access-date=5 February 2022|publisher=SCMP|date=6 February 2022}}{{Cite news|last=Chappell|first=Bill|date=2022-02-04|title=The Beijing Winter Olympics' cauldron lighting made a political statement|language=en|work=NPR|url=https://www.npr.org/2022/02/04/1078234213/beijing-olympics-flame-torch-uyghur|access-date=2022-02-04}}

Due to the backlash China received for the alleged Uyghur genocide, several Western media outlets speculated about the message China was intending to send with Dilnigeer's selection.{{Cite news|date=2022-02-05|title=What message did China send by choosing Uyghur torchbearer?|url=https://apnews.com/article/winter-olympics-uyghur-torchbearer-1f30da11687c7ff25ceedf651e5618a1|access-date=2022-02-05|website=AP News|language=en|archive-date=5 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205133816/https://apnews.com/article/winter-olympics-uyghur-torchbearer-1f30da11687c7ff25ceedf651e5618a1|url-status=live}}{{Cite news|last1=Buckley|first1=Chris|last2=Das|first2=Andrew|date=2022-02-04|title=In a provocative choice, China picks an athlete with a Uyghur name to help light the cauldron.|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/02/04/sports/olympics/cauldron-lighting-opening-ceremony-uyghur-china.html|access-date=2022-02-05|archive-date=5 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205123502/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/02/04/sports/olympics/cauldron-lighting-opening-ceremony-uyghur-china.html|url-status=live}}{{Cite news|last=Peters|first=Justin|date=2022-02-05|title=China's Opening Ceremony Taunted the World. What Is NBC Going to Do About It?|url=https://slate.com/culture/2022/02/nbc-winter-olympics-uyghur-torchbearer-opening-ceremony-beijing.html|access-date=2022-02-05|website=Slate Magazine|language=en|archive-date=5 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205193634/https://slate.com/culture/2022/02/nbc-winter-olympics-uyghur-torchbearer-opening-ceremony-beijing.html|url-status=live}}{{cite news|title=China's human rights record slammed as Beijing Olympics kick off|work=NBC Nightly News|last=Holt|first=Lester|date=2022-02-05|url=https://www.nbc.com/nbc-nightly-news/video/chinas-human-rights-record-slammed-as-beijing-olympics-kick-off/490821668|language=en-US|access-date=2022-02-05|archive-date=6 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220206052427/https://www.nbc.com/nbc-nightly-news/video/chinas-human-rights-record-slammed-as-beijing-olympics-kick-off/490821668|url-status=live}}{{Cite news|last=Chappell|first=Bill|date=2022-02-04|title=The Beijing Winter Olympics' cauldron lighting made a political statement|language=en|work=NPR|url=https://www.npr.org/2022/02/04/1078234213/beijing-olympics-flame-torch-uyghur|access-date=2022-02-04|archive-date=5 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205020818/https://www.npr.org/2022/02/04/1078234213/beijing-olympics-flame-torch-uyghur|url-status=live}}

On 26 January 2022, a spokesperson of China's Taiwan Affairs Office "incorrectly" called the Chinese Taipei (Taiwan) team "Taipei, China". Later that day, Taiwan announced that their Olympic team would not attend the opening and closing ceremonies in Beijing, formally due to anti-COVID-19 rules and delayed flights.{{cite news|last=Gibson|first=Liam|date=28 January 2022|title=Taiwan's Winter Olympic team will not attend ceremonies in Beijing|url=https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/4425730|work=[[Taiwan News]]|location=Taipei, Taiwan|access-date=28 January 2022|archive-date=29 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220129015840/https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/4425730|url-status=live}}{{cite news|language=zh|trans-title=Chinese Taipei delegation will not attend the Beijing Winter Olympics opening and closing ceremonies; Party and government figures: will be announced by the Ministry of Education|date=26 January 2022|title=北京冬奧我代表團不出席開閉幕式 黨政人士：將由教育部宣布|url=https://news.ltn.com.tw/news/politics/breakingnews/3814076|work=[[Liberty Times]]|access-date=26 January 2022}} The same day, another Taiwan official stated that Taiwan would be diplomatically boycotting the ceremonies as well.{{cite news|last1=Berkeley|first1=Geoff|title=Taiwan officials set to shun Beijing 2022 Ceremonies over propaganda fears|url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1118320/taiwan-officials-boycott-ceremonies|access-date=26 January 2022|agency=[[Insidethegames]]|date=26 January 2022|archive-date=26 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220126133515/https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1118320/taiwan-officials-boycott-ceremonies|url-status=live}} On 28 January 2022, a Taiwan official also stated concern that the Chinese Taipei (中华台北) and Hong Kong, China (中国香港) delegations would be adjacent to each other in the Parade of Nations due to the Chinese collation order, "downgrading" Taiwan's status.{{cite news|date=28 January 2022|title=Olympic-Team Taiwan won't be at Winter Games opening ceremony|url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/team-taiwan-wont-be-winter-games-opening-ceremony-2022-01-28/|work=[[Reuters]]|location=London, United Kingdom|access-date=28 January 2022|archive-date=28 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220128193350/https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/team-taiwan-wont-be-winter-games-opening-ceremony-2022-01-28/|url-status=live}}

Between 29 January and 31 January 2022, the International Olympic Committee repeatedly contacted the Chinese Taipei Olympic Committee, stating that it was obligated to attend the ceremonies to "comply with the Olympic Charter".{{cite web | url=https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/4427969 | title=IOC forces Taiwan's team to attend opening, closing ceremonies of Beijing Winter Olympics | Taiwan News | 2022-02-01 12:00:00 | date=February 2022 }} (The IOC had already suspended North Korea for not sending a team to the Tokyo Summer Games in violation of the Olympic Charter.) On 1 February 2022, Taiwanese officials relented on their boycott.{{cite news|title=Taiwan team relents, will attend Olympic ceremonies in China|url=https://apnews.com/article/sports-china-beijing-2020-tokyo-olympics-taiwan-212a92d8c1efdd3a4fb0f1a92835fcb1|access-date=4 February 2022|work=Associated Press|date=1 February 2022|archive-date=4 February 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220204140748/https://apnews.com/article/sports-china-beijing-2020-tokyo-olympics-taiwan-212a92d8c1efdd3a4fb0f1a92835fcb1|url-status=live }} According to attendees of the rehearsal of the opening ceremony, Japan and Chinese Taipei marched adjacently, followed by "a few" countries, followed by Hong Kong, preventing the Chinese Taipei and Hong Kong delegations from being adjacent.{{Cite web |url=http://www.uschinapress.com/static/content/SH/2022-01-29/936979897321402368.html |title=消息人士：北京冬奥开幕式，台运动员队名仍为"中华台北"-侨报网 |access-date=6 February 2022 |archive-date=6 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220206052418/http://www.uschinapress.com/static/content/SH/2022-01-29/936979897321402368.html |url-status=live }} However, during the actual opening ceremony, Japan, Chinese Taipei, and Hong Kong marched adjacently in that order.{{Cite web |url=https://flipr.com.ar/nacionales/ultimo-momento/a-collection-of-smaller-yet-interesting-moments-from-the-opening-ceremony-of-beijing-2022/ |title=Flipr - Tareas programadas |access-date=6 February 2022 |archive-date=6 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220206052435/https://flipr.com.ar/nacionales/ultimo-momento/a-collection-of-smaller-yet-interesting-moments-from-the-opening-ceremony-of-beijing-2022/ |url-status=live }}

On China's state media, the broadcast of the opening ceremony cut away to a clip of Xi Jinping when the Chinese Taipei delegation paraded, while the broadcast's commentator announced the delegation's name as "Taipei, China".{{Cite web |url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1118778/updates/71803 |title=Archived copy |access-date=6 February 2022 |archive-date=6 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220206052434/https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1118778/updates/71803 |url-status=live }}{{Cite web |url=https://time.com/6145179/beijing-olympics-opening-ceremony-politics/ |title=How China Leaned into Politics at the Beijing Olympics Opening Ceremony |date=4 February 2022 |access-date=6 February 2022 |archive-date=5 February 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220205113416/https://time.com/6145179/beijing-olympics-opening-ceremony-politics/ |url-status=live }}

Groups critical of China's human rights record, urged viewers to boycott the 2022 Games on television. In the United States, NBC's live broadcast of the ceremony was the lowest watched opening ceremony in U.S. history. TV coverage of the 2022 Games overall has continued to trend down in ratings since Pyeongchang 2018 and the Tokyo Games just six months prior, while streaming continued to see massive increases.{{cite web|url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1118867/nbc-records-lowest-viewing-figure-ever|title=Beijing 2022 sets record for lowest watched Opening Ceremony in history on NBC as campaigners urge viewers to boycott Games|last=Barker|first=Philip|date=6 February 2022|website=www.insidethegames.biz/|publisher=Dunsar Media Ltd.|access-date=6 February 2022}}{{cite news|last=Reedy|first=Joe|date=8 February 2022|title=Several factors contribute to NBC's low Olympic ratings|url=https://www.thestar.com/sports/olympics/2022/02/08/several-factors-contribute-to-nbcs-low-olympic-ratings.html|work=[[Toronto Star]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|location=Toronto, Ontario, Canada|access-date=8 February 2022}}

Some South Korean people were angered and accused China of appropriating Korean culture as their own, as one of the performers representing the ethnic Koreans in China wore a traditional choson-ot when delivering the national flag of China.{{cite web|url=https://www.insidethegames.biz/articles/1118863/moon-jae-in-beijing-2022-winter-olympics|title=South Korea accuse China of cultural misappropriation in Opening Ceremony, but President hopes Beijing 2022 can promote "peace and harmony"|last=Pavitt|first=Michael|date=6 February 2022|website=www.insidethegames.biz/|publisher=Dunsar Media Ltd.|access-date=6 February 2022}}{{Cite web|url= https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20220205002100315|title= S. Koreans up in arms over depiction of hanbok as Chinese during opening ceremony|work= Yonhap|date=2022-02-05|last=Yoo|first=Jee-ho}} Democratic Party presidential nominee Lee Jae-myung, People Power Party presidential nominee Yoon Suk-yeol, People's Party presidential candidate Ahn Cheol-soo joined the fray and expressed their discontent.{{Cite web|url= https://english.hani.co.kr/arti/english_edition/english_editorials/1030067.html|title= China should know why Koreans are upset over hanbok at Olympics show|date=2022-02-07|work=The Hankyoreh}} However some South Koreans felt their politicians' reactions were misguided, and say that it was clear to them, that the woman was representing the estimated 2 million ethnic Koreans who live in China.{{Cite web|title=S. Korea politicians criticize China over traditional dress|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/korea-politicians-criticize-china-traditional-dress-82690612|access-date=2022-02-13|website=ABC News|language=en}} The Chinese Embassy in South Korea responded that China respected the historical and cultural traditions of South Korea, and hanbok belongs to ethnic Koreans everywhere, including in China.{{Cite web|url= https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/chinese-embassy-defends-use-of-korean-dress-in-olympic-ceremony/47330482|title= Chinese Embassy defends use of Korean dress in Olympic ceremony|agency= Reuters|date=2022-02-08}}

Opening Ceremony
Category:Ceremonies in China
Category:Olympics opening ceremonies
Category:Zhang Yimou

During the Parade of Nations within the Beijing 2022 Winter Olympics opening ceremony on February 4, athletes and officials from each participating country marched in the Beijing National Stadium preceded by their flag and placard bearer bearing the respective country's name. Each flag bearer was chosen either by the nation's National Olympic Committee or by the team of athletes themselves.

Athletes entered the stadium in an order dictated by the Olympic tradition. As the originator of the Olympics, the Greek team entered first.{{cite news|last2=Davis|first2=Scott|last1=Gaines|first1=Cork|date=9 February 2018|title=Why Greece always leads the parade of athletes at the Olympic opening ceremony and how the rest of the order is determined|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/greece-rio-olympics-opening-ceremony-parade-2016-8|work=[[Business Insider]]|location=New York City, New York, U.S.|access-date=15 January 2021}}

Countries marched in order of the Chinese language.{{cite magazine|last=Steger|first=Isabella|date=4 February 2022|title=Here's the Order of Countries at the Beijing Olympics Opening Ceremony|url=https://time.com/6145111/order-of-countries-opening-ceremony-2022-olympics/|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|location=New York City, New York, US|access-date=8 February 2022}} The collation method used was based on the names as written in Simplified Chinese characters and is similar to that used in Chinese dictionaries. The names were sorted by the number of strokes in the first character of the name, then by the stroke order of the character (in the order 橫竖撇捺折, c.f. Wubi method), then the number of strokes and stroke order of the second character, then next character and so on.{{Cite news|last1=Mather|first1=Victor|last2=Buckley|first2=Chris|date=4 February 2022|title=The Chinese language determines the order of the Parade of Nations.|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/02/04/sports/opening-ceremony-order-of-countries.html|access-date=4 February 2022|issn=0362-4331}}  For example, this placed San Marino () in 28th position, just ahead of Kyrgyzstan () because the initial character for "San Marino" () is written in 5 strokes, while that for "Kyrgyzstan" () is written in 6 strokes.

The country that will host the next Winter Olympics, Italy, marched before the host nation China entered, instead of entering between New Zealand and Serbia, according to the Chinese collation order.{{cite web|url=https://olympics.com/ioc/news/future-olympic-hosts-to-gain-prominence-in-athletes-parades|title=Future Olympic hosts to gain prominence in athletes' parades|date=3 December 2019|website=www.olympics.com/|publisher=[[International Olympic Committee]]|access-date=15 January 2021}}
As part of its doping penalty, Russia competes under the acronym "ROC" and the flag of the Russian Olympic Committee, and the name of the committee in full cannot be used to refer to the delegation.

Announcers in the stadium read off the names of the marching nations in Mandarin Chinese (the official language of the host country), English and French (the official languages of the Olympics) with music accompanying the athletes as they marched into the stadium.
According to the current version of the Olympic Charter, each nation had the option of having two flag bearers (a man and a woman) in an effort to promote gender equality.

The following is a list of each country's flag bearer. The list is sorted by the sequence that each nation appeared in the Parade of Nations.{{cite web|date=February 4, 2022|title=When does each country march during Winter Olympics Opening Ceremony?|url=https://www.cbs8.com/article/sports/olympics/beijing-olympics-opening-ceremony-parade-of-nations-order/507-184d5dfa-dbd4-4e22-8bfb-6c47c1137996|access-date=2022-02-04|website=cbs8.com|language=en-US}} The names are given in their official designations by the IOC, and the Chinese names follow their official designations by the Beijing Organizing Committee for the 2022 Olympic and Paralympic Winter Games.

The 2022 Winter Olympics torch relay was run from 18 October 2021 until 4 February 2022. After it was lit in Olympia, Greece, the torch traveled in a symbolic relay[https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/olympics/weather-protest-cloud-beijing-flame-lighting-rehearsal/2021/10/17/01ab4854-2f3a-11ec-8036-7db255bff176_story.html ''Weather, protest, cloud - Beijing flame-lighting rehearsal'']{{Dead link|date=June 2022 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}, washingtonpost.com, Sunday, October 17, 2021, to Athens on 19 October.{{Cite web |url=https://hoc.gr/en/node/3188 |title=The Olympic flame lighting ceremony for the Beijing 2022 Games will take place on 18 October 2021 |website=Hellenic Olympic Committee |access-date=25 September 2021 |archive-date=25 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210925015543/https://hoc.gr/en/node/3188 |url-status=live }}{{Cite web |url=http://www.china.org.cn/sports/2021-09/24/content_77771600.htm |title=2022 Olympic flame to be lit in Greece without spectators |website=www.china.org.cn |access-date=25 September 2021 |archive-date=25 September 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210925015528/http://www.china.org.cn/sports/2021-09/24/content_77771600.htm |url-status=live }} The Chinese leg ended in Beijing National Stadium, at the end of the opening ceremony. On 20 October 2021, it was announced that the Chinese leg will have only three days, following a series of displays of the flame in various Chinese cities, starting on 2 February, at the morning of the first day of the Chinese New Year as stage 3. Unlike the previous relays, the relay only visited the three venues clusters, the main sights of Beijing and the city of Zhangjiakou.{{cite web|url=https://www.beijing2022.cn/sv1/wog/wap.htm#/20211020003733/20211020003733|title=北京2022年冬奥会火种欢迎仪式在京举行|work=Beijing2022.cn|access-date=20 October 2021|archive-date=18 August 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210818224851/https://www.beijing2022.cn/sv1/wog/wap.htm#/20211020003733/20211020003733|url-status=dead}} The final torch was lit by long-distance runner Dilnigar Ilhamjan (Dinige'er Yilamujiang) and nordic combined Zhao Jiawen.

Activists staged a protest at the Olympic torch lighting ceremony in Greece.{{cite web |last1=O'Donnell |first1=Noreen |title=Uyghurs, Tibetans, Hong Kongers Join Together to Protest Beijing Olympics |url=https://www.nbcchicago.com/news/national-international/uyghurs-tibetans-hong-kongers-join-together-to-protest-beijing-olympics/2741321/ |website=nbcchicago.com |date=28 January 2022 |publisher=NBC Chicago |access-date=31 January 2022}}

The choice to have Qi Fabao, a People's Liberation Army commander famous for his participation in the 2020–2021 China–India skirmishes, be a torchbearer has been controversial with India launching a diplomatic boycott of the games as a result.{{cite web |last1=Ramachandran |first1=Sudha |title=India Joins Diplomatic Boycott of Beijing Winter Olympics |url=https://thediplomat.com/2022/02/india-joins-diplomatic-boycott-of-beijing-winter-olympics/ |website=thediplomat.com |publisher=The Diplomat |access-date=3 February 2022}}

The relay ended after the 2022 Winter Olympics opening ceremony, when the Olympic Cauldron was lit by Altay Uyghur cross-country skier Dilnigar Ilhamjan, and nordic combined Zhao Jiawen.
After the cauldron in the stadium was lit, the three venues clusters' cauldron was lit right after the end of the opening ceremony.
